headline: A mitigation working group meets daily across fifteen strands of activity
detail: Deans, heads of department, senior management and Students' Union UCL, meeting daily, with Education Committee weekly.
quote: The working group of Deans, Heads of Department, members of the senior management team and Students’ Union UCL has been established to mitigate the short and longer term risks to the university across 15 strands of activity.
notes: The fifteen strands are the earliest statement of what UCL thought was at risk. Issue 2 records the group meeting daily and Education Committee weekly.

headline: Campus remains open on Public Health England advice
detail: UCL's opening position: follow PHE, NHS and FCO advice rather than act independently.
quote: On the advice of PHE, the university remains open and we recommend that students, staff and visitors attend their scheduled activities as normal.
notes: The baseline against which every later closure is measured. Four days later face-to-face teaching ceased.

headline: UCL begins a daily coronavirus update for staff
detail: The first of what became 165 numbered issues, running to 4 May 2022. The stated reason is that the situation was changing faster than the FAQ page could carry.
quote: we have decided to issue a daily update for the time being
notes: The newsletter series begins seven months before the case statistics, which start 2020-10-09. The timeline's first act has no data track.

headline: Students who choose not to attend teaching will not be penalised
detail: Teaching continued in person, but attendance stopped being compulsory. The first crack in normal operation.
quote: UCL will not penalise any students who choose not to attend teaching events

headline: UCL advises against all international UCL trips
detail: Applied in both directions and to contractors and visitors as well as staff and students.
quote: UCL is advising against all international UCL trips for staff, undergraduate students, contractors and visitors, in-bound and out-bound

headline: International travel on UCL business halted until 1 May
detail: Advice of the previous day hardened into an instruction, with delegations cancelled and incoming visitors postponed.
quote: As of today, staff and students should not travel internationally on UCL business until 1 May 2020
notes: Same day the WHO declared a pandemic. Whether UCL was responding to that is not stated in the newsletter and should not be asserted.

headline: First confirmed coronavirus case in the UCL community
detail: A student, reported to staff on 12 March and referred back to in issue 5 the following day.
quote: I wrote to you yesterday to let you know that one of our students has tested positive for coronavirus (Covid-19).
notes: Filed on 12 March, the date of the event, though the source is the newsletter of 13 March. Seven months before the case statistics begin, so this case appears in no dataset.

headline: Study Abroad and affiliate students formally recalled
detail: Students already overseas were asked to return to the UK or their home country; those about to depart were told not to go.
quote: the university is formally recalling students who are taking part in Study Abroad, Double or Dual degree, or international Affiliate programmes

headline: UCL-managed halls to stay open all year even if UCL closes
detail: An early and load-bearing commitment: accommodation was decoupled from campus operation from the outset.
quote: all UCL-managed halls will remain open as usual throughout the year, even if UCL is closed
notes: Held to. Eight days later students were urged to leave, but the halls stayed open for those with nowhere to go.

headline: Walk-in service at the partner GP surgery suspended
detail: Ridgmount Practice moved to telephone triage on PHE advice.
quote: the walk-in service at Ridgmount Practice (UCL's partner GP surgery) is suspended until further notice

headline: All term 3 teaching to be delivered online via Moodle
detail: Decided in March for a term beginning in April, so UCL had committed to a remote summer term before the first lockdown began.
quote: All teaching in term 3 will be delivered online via Moodle as far as possible.

headline: Alternative assessment replaces exams for taught students
detail: Open-book assessment and coursework, so that students could complete the year away from campus.
quote: Alternative forms of assessment will be put in place for all other taught students, such as open book assessments and further coursework, to enable students to complete assessments away from the university.

headline: Clinical academics released to support the NHS
detail: A standing release rather than a case-by-case one, and the first of UCL's civic contributions in the record.
quote: Not only have we agreed to release all our clinical academics from their UCL responsibilities if they wish to support the NHS service during the coronavirus outbreak
notes: Category civic, so that the civic contributions can be filtered out of the lag analysis. See TIMELINE-PLAN.md open question 3.

headline: Face-to-face teaching ceases; teaching moves online from 16 March
detail: Approved by Academic Committee on 13 March and announced the same day in both the Provost's View and issue 5.
quote: Face-to-face teaching will cease with effect from today, 13 March, with as much teaching as possible moving online from Monday 16 March until the end of term 2.
notes: Ten days before the national lockdown of 23 March 2020, and the clearest case in the record of UCL acting ahead of national policy. The lag is negative. Also carried verbatim in issue 5 the same day.

headline: Formal assessment for first-year undergraduates to be reduced
detail: Framed as reducing the burden on staff rather than on students.
quote: We will seek to significantly reduce the amount of further formal assessment for first-year undergraduates this year.
notes: Hardened a week later into outright cancellation and a pass/fail capstone.

headline: Second confirmed case at UCL, a contractor's employee
detail: Reported the day after the first student case.
quote: we have been notified today of a further case
notes: UCL was naming individual cases at this stage. By October 2020 it was publishing aggregate counts, which is the series the archive preserves.

headline: All staff able to work remotely told to do so from 17 March
detail: Campus stayed open for those who could not work from home.
quote: Although campus remains open, all staff who are able to work remotely should do so from tomorrow, Tuesday 17 March.
notes: Announced 16 March, effective 17 March. The one-day gap is why date_kind exists.

headline: External events suspended and the theatre, galleries and museums closed
detail: Covered offer-holder events, the Bloomsbury Theatre, all UCL galleries and museums, and staff recruitment that could not be held remotely.
quote: As of today, Monday 16 March, all external events are suspended until 1 May.
notes: The 1 May horizon recurs across March 2020 decisions and is consistently too optimistic.

headline: Staff over 70 or with health conditions must work from home
detail: An instruction rather than advice, extended to those living with or caring for people at higher risk.
quote: All staff aged over 70 and those with pre-existing health conditions must work from home.
notes: Predates the national shielding programme, which opened to letters from 21 March 2020. Needs checking against the primary record in stage 2 before the comparison is made in the rendering.

headline: Coronavirus sickness absence exempted from absence triggers and paid in full
detail: Regardless of length of service or sick pay status.
quote: sickness absence for coronavirus will not count towards the number of days’ absence which would trigger a formal process for managing absence under our usual policy

headline: Remote working extended to research, facilities and services
detail: The Provost's own decision, taken in response to the government's recommendation of the previous evening.
quote: In light of the government’s recommendation, I have taken the decision to extend remote working to all of our research as well as facilities and services.
notes: An explicit statement of national policy being the cause, which is rarer in the record than one might expect and is what makes this row usable for lag analysis.

headline: Students strongly advised to return home
detail: With accommodation offered to any student unable to travel.
quote: We now strongly advise all students to return home as soon as they can, as we are aware that travel will become more restrictive in the coming days and weeks.
notes: Six days before the national lockdown, and anticipating the travel restrictions rather than following them.

headline: Summer placements, summer schools and pre-sessional teaching cancelled
quote: all summer placements, summer schools and pre-sessional teaching have now been cancelled

headline: UCL to stay on a remote working footing until 15 April
detail: Explicitly framed as not a closure, with teaching, assessment and research continuing remotely.
quote: The university will remain on a remote working footing until 15 April 2020, after the Easter closure.
notes: The stated end date passed without campus reopening. The horizon UCL set in March was wrong by more than a year for most activity.

headline: The Prime Minister announces the closure of schools for most pupils
detail: Schools closed at the end of Friday 20 March and did not reopen on Monday 23 March, which is why the newsletters and this source date the same measure differently.
quote: announcing closure of schools for most pupils from 23 March
notes: UCL restricted its Day Nursery to national-interest and essential staff the next day, a lag of one. The UCL note described this as closure "by 20 March" and the Commons Library timeline as closure "from 23 March"; both describe the same break, from opposite ends of the weekend.

headline: All library loans renewed to 5 June and recalls suspended
quote: We arranged yesterday to renew all books on loan until 5 June and all recalls have been suspended.

headline: Mitigation group restructured into subgroups under the Provost
detail: With trade union and Students' Union representation, and epidemiological advice from Professor Andrew Hayward.
quote: The Coronavirus Mitigation Group is assuming a new structure to allow us to continue our meetings effectively and make timely decisions while staff are working remotely.
notes: Effective 20 March per issue 9. The decision-making structure itself changed to survive remote working.

headline: Day Nursery to stay open only for national-interest and essential staff
detail: Narrowed from the previous week's position that it remained open to all staff and students.
quote: The UCL Day Nursery will stay open as long as possible for the children of staff undertaking research in the immediate national interest or whose work onsite is essential to the continued operation of the university.
notes: Follows the government's announcement of 18 March that schools and nurseries would close by 20 March. A one-day lag.

headline: Staff with caring responsibilities to keep normal pay without taking leave
quote: Please be assured that we wish to support you and will understand that you may have to change work routines, take holiday at short notice and perhaps not work your normal number of hours.
notes: Restated more firmly on 23 March: caring for dependents became an authorised absence.

headline: First-year undergraduate assessments cancelled and replaced by a capstone
detail: A single pass/fail piece of reflective work with a late June deadline, required to progress to year two.
quote: On Friday 20 March, we contacted all undergraduate first year students to tell them their assessments have been cancelled.
notes: Filed on 20 March, the date of the action; the source is issue 11 of 23 March, which reports it retrospectively. Students had petitioned for deferral instead and UCL declined.

headline: Most UCL buildings and all libraries close
detail: The Student Centre, accommodation services, some residences and buildings supporting essential research stayed open.
quote: To facilitate the latter, the Student Centre, UCL Accommodation services, some student residences and buildings linked to essential research will remain open. All other UCL buildings and libraries will be closed.
notes: Three days before the national lockdown. The Student Centre closed on 24 March, the day after it.

headline: Only research in the immediate national interest may continue on site
detail: Announced 17 March with a deadline of 5.30pm on Friday 20 March.
quote: From the end of Friday, the only research that will take place in our buildings will be in the immediate national interest, for example work on coronavirus.
notes: Filed on the effective date, 20 March; announced 17 March. Faculties coordinated the shutdown of experiments in the intervening three days.

headline: Students may self-certify extenuating circumstances for the rest of the year
quote: UCL has agreed that students can self-certify if they have Extenuating Circumstances for the remainder of the 2019/20 academic year.

headline: Students urged to vacate halls; no Term 3 accommodation fees
detail: Halls stayed open for students with nowhere else to go, consistent with the commitment given on 12 March.
quote: we have urged students who have access to an alternative safe and secure source of accommodation to vacate UCL halls of residences
notes: The fee waiver applied to students who had already checked out as well as those planning to.

headline: UCL PCR machines made available to the NHS for testing
detail: Alongside medical students volunteering and clinical academics released to the NHS.
quote: We are also making UCL’s Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) machines available to the NHS to expand the capacity for coronavirus testing.

headline: The Prime Minister announces the first national lockdown
detail: Announced on the evening of 23 March; the measures became law three days later.
quote: PM announces the first lockdown in the UK, ordering people to “stay at home”
notes: The counterpart for five UCL rows, and the anchor of the lag analysis in both directions. UCL had already stopped face-to-face teaching ten days earlier and barred staff from campus the day after this.

headline: All staff must work from home; campus only for key workers
detail: Campus access restricted to key workers and Dean-authorised national-interest research.
quote: All staff must work from home wherever possible. This is to limit the spread of infection to you and to others.
notes: Published the same day as the national lockdown announcement, but the substance had been in force since 20 March. The national announcement came in the evening; issue 12 the next day is the response to it.

headline: Contractor staff get sick pay from the first day of absence
detail: Axis, Sodexo and Aramark staff brought into line with directly employed staff. Agreed with UNISON for July and brought forward.
quote: staff employed by UCL’s suppliers Axis, Sodexo and Aramark will be able to access sick pay from the first day of an absence, in line with staff employed directly by the university
notes: Announced 20 March, effective 23 March. UCL contractors also honoured all contracted hours whether staff worked or not.

headline: Day Nursery fees refunded and places held during closure
quote: fees paid in advance for the period from 23 March 2020 will be refunded. Further fees will not be collected during this period, but all places will be held until the nursery is able to open again.
notes: Filed on 23 March, the date the refund period begins; announced in issue 20 of 3 April.

headline: UCL joins the national coronavirus genome sequencing consortium
detail: Professor Judith Breuer of the UCL Pathogen Genomics Unit named among the scientists mapping the spread of the virus.
quote: Professor Judith Breuer, Director of UCL Pathogen Genomics Unit (UCL-PGU), has been announced as one of the leading UK scientists to be part of a major new genome sequencing consortium which will map the spread of coronavirus.
notes: The consortium is COG-UK, though the newsletter does not name it. Do not add the name to the ledger without a primary source.

headline: Staff must not attend campus unless authorised key workers
detail: UCL's direct response to the stay-at-home order announced the previous evening, with authorisation letters and ID required.
quote: Following yesterday’s announcement by the UK Government requiring everyone to stay at home, you must not now physically come into work unless you are one of our authorised key workers and/or you are undertaking research in the immediate national interest.
notes: One day after the national announcement of 23 March 2020. The clearest positive lag in the record and the counterpart to the negative lag of 13 March.

headline: The Student Centre closes and Bidborough House is restricted
detail: The last general-access buildings shut, four days after the main closure.
quote: The Student Centre is now closed. Bidborough House also has very limited access and only for key workers and those undertaking research in the national interest.
notes: On 23 March the Student Centre was still open for staff who could not work at home. The national order closed it.

headline: REF 2021 data submission postponed by the funding bodies
quote: The funding bodies have agreed to postpone the Research Excellence Framework 2021 data submission until further notice.
notes: A sector-level decision reported by UCL. The sector track should carry the funding bodies' own announcement once retrieved in stage 2; this row records UCL relaying it.

headline: The first lockdown measures come into force
detail: Three days after the announcement.
quote: Lockdown measures legally come into force
notes: The gap between announcement and legal force is why the ledger separates announced from effective dates.

headline: Remote, Not Distant at UCL launched to support remote working
detail: An HR website covering workspace setup, staying connected, managing teams remotely and mental health. It recurs in the newsletters for the next two years.
quote: today colleagues in Human Resources have launched Remote, Not Distant at UCL , a new website to help you and those around you adapt to remote working
notes: The start date of a recurring thread, which the plan's inclusion test admits even though the later repetitions do not earn rows.

headline: Students in shared-bathroom halls moved to en-suite rooms on PHE advice
detail: So that a student who fell ill could self-isolate without exposing others. No extra fees, and UCL arranged the moves.
quote: On the advice of Public Health England, we are relocating some students who are staying with us in UCL halls and are currently living in accommodation with shared bathrooms to halls with en-suite facilities.
notes: An infection-control measure inside UCL's own estate, distinct from the national restrictions, and among the earliest.

headline: Students told alternative assessments will be confirmed by 6 April
detail: With an assurance that no assessment would fall earlier than previously advertised.
quote: We have told students that they will receive more information about their assessments by 6 April 2020.
notes: Filed on 27 March, the date students were contacted; reported in issue 16 of 30 March.

headline: UCL Together launched to redeploy staff to teams needing support
detail: An HR initiative matching volunteers to teams under pressure, and to the NHS and emergency services outside UCL. Individual registration opened 30 March.
quote: colleagues in Human Resources have developed UCL Together, a new initiative to connect teams in need of more support, with offers of help from other areas of the university

headline: UCL laboratories donate nitrile gloves to UCLH
detail: Collected at the North Lodge on Gower Street for delivery to the hospital.
quote: UCL staff working in our laboratories are donating supplies of nitrile gloves to UCLH, which is in urgent need of Personal Protective Equipment for NHS workers treating coronavirus patients.

headline: All 2020 graduation ceremonies cancelled
detail: June, July and September 2020 ceremonies, with an alternative celebration promised for the following year.
quote: All graduation ceremonies this year have been cancelled. This covers ceremonies in June, July and September 2020.

headline: UCL-Ventura breathing aid approved for NHS use in ten days
detail: Developed by UCL engineers with Mercedes Formula One and UCLH clinicians. One hundred devices sent to UCLH for trials.
quote: UCL engineers have worked with Mercedes Formula One and clinicians at UCLH to produce a breathing aid that can help coronavirus patients stay out of intensive care. The device was developed and approved for use in the NHS in just ten days
notes: The single most visible UCL civic contribution of the pandemic. Category civic so it can be filtered out of the lag analysis.

headline: Government orders up to 10,000 UCL-Ventura breathing aids
detail: Two days after regulatory approval, with mass production targeted for the following week.
quote: The Government has now ordered up to 10,000 of the devices, known as UCL-Ventura, which gained regulatory approval for use in the NHS in just ten days.

headline: Over 300 final-year medical students fast-tracked into the NHS
detail: Part of the government's response; around 200 were already volunteering.
quote: More than 300 of UCL’s final year medical students are being fast-tracked through graduation this week, ready to be made frontline NHS doctors, as part of the Government’s response to the coronavirus outbreak.

headline: Pay deductions for March strike action cancelled
detail: Framed as recognition of the effort staff were making to move teaching and assessment online.
quote: We have agreed to cancel the payroll deductions for all strike action taken by staff in March, in recognition of the incredible contribution that our people are making in these very challenging circumstances.
notes: The UCU strike ran into March 2020 and was called off as the pandemic took hold, noted in issue 10.

headline: Buildings to stay closed after Easter, with a review on 1 May
detail: The first of many review dates that passed without reopening.
quote: In line with Government advice, UCL buildings will remain closed after the Easter break and you should continue to work remotely until further notice, unless you are one of our key workers. We will review this decision on 1 May
notes: Explicitly attributed to government advice, so usable for lag analysis.

headline: Final-year PGR writing-up extended and hardship fund raised to £3,000
detail: With UCL lobbying UKRI, Wellcome and government through the Russell Group for sector-wide support.
quote: We’ve agreed that the writing-up period for all PGR students in their final year will be extended, and we’ve also agreed to ensure that the hardship fund will support those students in need for the duration of the crisis, with an increase in the amount claimable to £3,000.

headline: Disturbance allowance introduced for on-site key workers
detail: £350, £175 or £75 a month by days on site, extended to clinical staff seconded to the NHS, temporary staff and outsourced workers.
quote: our onsite key workers will receive a disturbance allowance in addition to their usual pay
notes: One of the few decisions in the record that treats the people who could not work from home as a distinct group.

headline: Term 4 accommodation fees waived as well as Term 3
quote: We will not be charging accommodation fees for students for this Term 4 period who will no longer be staying with us, as we have done for the Term 3 period.

headline: UCL adopts a no-detriment principle for summer assessments
detail: Exceptional amendments to Academic Regulations, guaranteeing classifications at least in line with work to date.
quote: We have written to all students to let them know that UCL has adopted a “no detriment” principle, which recognises students’ academic performance so far and ensures that academic outcomes won’t be negatively impacted by the alternative assessments due to take place this summer.

headline: UCL-Ventura designs released worldwide free of charge
detail: Published so manufacturers anywhere could produce the device.
quote: All the details required to make the UCL-Ventura device have now been made available online and at no cost so it can be produced by manufacturers around the world.
notes: By the following day 233 download requests had come from 25 countries.

headline: Annual leave carry-over raised from five days to seven
detail: A one-off change for the year, with no limit for key workers who had worked throughout.
quote: UCL has increased the number of days of annual leave that can be carried forward from this leave period to the next, from five to seven.

headline: Cyber-attacks on universities reported up 37% since the outbreak
detail: UCL identified its high-profile pandemic work as raising its own exposure.
quote: there has been a significant increase in cyber-attacks on universities, with some reports showing an increase of 37% above previous levels
notes: UCL is relaying an external claim without attributing it. Do not repeat the 37% figure as established. Checked twice and still unattributable: the newsletter names no source, and the archive's inventory of every link in that issue shows the only security link goes to UCL's own Stay Secure pages. There is no trail to follow, which is itself the finding. This is the one claim of the three stage 1 flagged that could not be verified.

headline: Travel restrictions extended to 1 August after FCO advice
detail: Following the FCO advising against all but essential international travel indefinitely. UCL stopped accepting expense claims for travel booked from that day.
quote: In light of this advice, UCL is extending its travel restrictions as of today. Staff and students should not travel internationally on UCL business until 1 August 2020 .
notes: A direct extension of the 11 March restriction, whose original horizon of 1 May had become untenable. Names the FCO advice as the cause.

headline: Copyright restrictions relaxed so teaching material could be digitised
quote: Some copyright restrictions have been temporarily relaxed to allow more educational material to be digitised and made available online, to support taught courses during the pandemic.
notes: A sector-level change UCL is relaying, not a UCL decision. The publishers' and Jisc side belongs on the sector track if it is retrieved in stage 2.

headline: Assessment programme confirmed: 3,333 assessments across 2,367 modules adjusted
detail: Equating to 130,000 individual student assessments, 31% of the total. Of 2,000 invigilated exams, 1,061 became coursework, 667 became 24-hour timed exams, 237 were excluded and 40 deferred.
quote: In total, 3,333 assessments across 2,367 modules have been adjusted, equating to 130,000 individual student assessments – or 31% of the total.
notes: The clearest quantification in the whole record of what moving a university online actually cost in work.

headline: Gold, Silver and Bronze crisis structure endorsed by UCL Council
detail: Led by the Provost and covering business continuity, education, research and external engagement.
quote: A new Gold / Silver / Bronze structure, led directly by me and endorsed by UCL Council, our governing body, has been in place for several weeks and is functioning well.
notes: The emergency-services command model, adopted by a university. Supersedes the mitigation-group structure of 18 March.

headline: Coronavirus: The Whole Story podcast launched
detail: A weekly podcast presented by Vivienne Parry, running through the pandemic and referenced in newsletters for the next two years.
quote: Coronavirus: The Whole Story is UCL’s new weekly podcast that explores the pandemic from the perspective of researchers across UCL.
notes: First appearance of a recurring thread, so it earns a row; the later weekly mentions do not.

headline: Grand Challenges initiative on recovery from Covid-19 opened
detail: Expressions of interest to 4 May 2020, aimed at researchers unable to continue their usual work.
quote: UCL Grand Challenges invites you to engage with our new initiative to address the urgent issues posed by the coronavirus outbreak.

headline: PhD students given automatic writing-up extensions and stipend underwriting
detail: Financial Assistance Fund raised to £3,000, a new Emergency Assistance Grant of up to £500, and final-year funded students underwritten at the minimum UKRI rate for up to three months.
quote: We are also providing all PhD students with an automatic writing-up (CRS) extension to cover the closure period.
notes: UCL acting ahead of the funders while lobbying them, which the Provost states explicitly: this is not a problem UCL can solve on its own.

headline: Learning Opportunities Fund reopened for students affected by strike action
detail: Grants of up to £500 for students whose learning was disrupted by the industrial action of 24 February to 20 March 2020.
quote: The Learning Opportunities Fund has reopened for applications from students whose learning was affected by the strike action that took place between 24 February and 20 March 2020.
notes: A pre-pandemic disruption being settled during the pandemic. The strike ended four days before the national lockdown.

headline: Biosafety guidance approved for work with coronavirus samples
detail: Covering research using samples from confirmed or suspected patients and work with the virus directly.
quote: The UCL Genetic Modification & Biosafety Committee has approved new guidance for those planning to work with samples from confirmed or suspected coronavirus patients, or those planning to work with the virus directly.

headline: UCL Together has supplied 497 days of redeployed support in four weeks
quote: To date, we have provided 497 days of additional support to teams across the university by matching volunteers to those departments who have requested help.
notes: A measured outcome for the scheme launched on 27 March, which is rare in the record; most initiatives are announced and never quantified.

headline: Recruitment freeze and capital spending paused as income falls
detail: With drastic cuts to non-pay expenditure to build cash reserves, and additional borrowing drawn down.
quote: We have, of course, taken immediate action to cut costs: introducing a recruitment freeze (so we prioritise those who are already part of our community); pausing or cancelling significant elements of capital expenditure
notes: The pivot from crisis response to financial survival, one month into lockdown.

headline: Single-year budgeting adopted with the contribution model set aside
detail: Normal processes suspended through Term 1, pending clarity on tuition fee income.
quote: We will do single-year budgeting, in which we set temporarily aside our usual processes through Term 1.

headline: UCL declines an across-the-board pay freeze adopted by other universities
quote: You may be aware that other universities have announced an across-the-board pay freeze. This is something that we are not yet considering and we will exhaust all other options before we do so.
notes: A rare explicit contrast with sector practice, and one the sector track should be able to test once the comparator institutions are identified in stage 2.

headline: Looking out for our students phone campaign launched
detail: Staff volunteers calling students to check how they were coping, committing at least one day a week to the end of May.
quote: Colleagues from across UCL have launched ‘Looking out for our students’, a new phone call campaign to keep in touch with our students and help them feel cared for during the coronavirus outbreak.

headline: Building closures to be reviewed on 8 May, with 15 May the earliest reopening
detail: Explicitly contingent on whether the national lockdown was extended again.
quote: We will review our building closures and remote working policy again on Friday 8 May, and the earliest date that we could start reopening our buildings would be Friday 15 May.
notes: The second review date to pass without reopening, after 1 May. Campus did not reopen to most staff in 2020 at all.

headline: Furloughed staff barred from any work, including writing up UCL results
quote: It is important to note that any staff on furlough cannot undertake any work for UCL. This means that activities such as writing up results obtained at UCL and analysing UCL data are not allowed.
notes: A condition of the national scheme with a sharp effect on research careers, and the clearest instance in the record of national policy constraining UCL rather than merely prompting it.

headline: Grant-funded staff offered furlough with UCL topping pay up to 100%
detail: Staff due to leave in May or June had leaving dates extended to the end of June; those due to leave in July or August were extended to the end of August on core funding.
quote: We will offer those grant-funded staff who were expecting to depart UCL during May and June 2020 the opportunity to be furloughed, and have their leaving date extended until the end of June.
notes: UCL's use of the national Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme. The newsletter notes the government share fell to about 60% in higher education because of pension arrangements, and that UCL made up the difference.

headline: Self-funded PhD students given until 31 July to pay final fee instalment
detail: Extended from 2 May, alongside Financial Assistance Fund grants of up to £3,000 prioritised for self-funders.
quote: the third and final instalment of tuition fees has now been extended from 2 May until 31 July 2020

headline: UCL-Ventura designs downloaded by over 1,800 teams in 105 countries
detail: Twenty-four days after the designs were released free of charge, with prototypes built in Mexico, South Africa, Canada, Bulgaria and Russia.
quote: In the 24 days since they were published, the designs have been downloaded by over 1,800 teams in 105 countries, representing non-profits, manufacturers, health experts and research institutes.

headline: Extenuating circumstances self-certified with no evidence required
detail: Introduced immediately before the summer assessment period began.
quote: changes have been made to UCL’s Extenuating Circumstances process, to reduce any burden on our students. Students can now self-certify and no longer need to provide evidence when applying.
notes: Extends the self-certification agreed on 20 March by removing the evidence requirement entirely.

headline: ONS finds Black adults far likelier to die of COVID-19 after adjusting for age
detail: Deaths from 2 March to 10 April 2020 in England and Wales. The published figures are 4.2 for Black males and 4.3 for Black females against White males and females.
quote: When taking into account age in the analysis, Black males are 4.2 times more likely to die from a COVID-19-related death and Black females are 4.3 times more likely than White ethnicity males and females
notes: UCL relayed this on 2 June 2020 and stage 1 flagged it as not to be repeated until the primary source was checked. It checks out: UCL's "four times" is a fair reading of 4.2 and 4.3. The ONS analysis adjusts for age only; the publication is explicit that it does not by itself establish cause.

headline: Faculties told to decide which modules not to run in 2020-21
detail: Faculty Delivery Teams identifying modules best suited to online delivery rather than moving everything online.
quote: An excellent teaching programme for 2020-21 will necessarily be different from what we might have planned in more conventional times – and will require decisions about what not to run.

headline: Gold team has post-lockdown plans ready ahead of the government announcement
detail: Prepared in advance of the Prime Minister's expected statement on easing restrictions.
quote: UCL’s Gold team has developed plans for post-lockdown operations and an action plan has been considered over the last couple of weeks, which will be updated as soon as there is any Government announcement.
notes: Evidence of UCL preparing before rather than after a national announcement, which is what the lag analysis is meant to distinguish. The response itself came on 11 May, one day after the announcement of 10 May.

headline: Provost asks staff to prioritise education over research for the crisis period
detail: With an assurance that the prioritisation would be recognised in appraisals and promotion cases.
quote: For this crisis period, I find myself needing to go further to ask you to prioritise education for the next few months, wherever and however you can.
notes: Justified in the same message by the dependence of research funding on overseas tuition fee income, which is the plainest statement in the record of why the teaching decisions mattered financially.

headline: The Prime Minister announces a conditional plan for lifting the lockdown
detail: The first easing of the first lockdown, including a return to the workplace for those who could not work from home.
quote: PM announces a conditional plan for lifting lockdown, and says that people who cannot work from home should return to the workplace but avoid public transport
notes: UCL diverged from this the next day, asking staff not to return to campus. That is the clearest case in the record of UCL declining an easing rather than following one.

headline: First timed alternative assessments taken by over 800 students
detail: Nineteen papers released on 11 May, the first test of the assessment redesign agreed in March.
quote: Over 800 students tackled one of 19 papers released yesterday.
notes: Filed on 11 May, the date of the assessments; reported in issue 42 of 12 May. Roughly eight weeks from the decision of 13 March to the first paper sat.

headline: No member of staff to be compelled to return for the pilots
detail: Transport, caring responsibilities and health concerns all accepted as reasons to decline.
quote: Please be assured that no one will be compelled to return to UCL for the pilots.

headline: Phased return to begin with a small number of pilots, most likely in June
detail: Aimed at laboratory and research work that could not be done from home, with nobody compelled to take part.
quote: The first stage of reopening will comprise a small number of pilots, where we will consult with colleagues in specific areas to identify opportunities to start working on campus again, most likely in June.

headline: Reopening made explicitly conditional on the national reproduction number
quote: If the rate of infection (R) rises again nationally, then we acknowledge that we may have to row back on this cautious reopening plan.
notes: The clearest statement in the record that UCL's campus policy was indexed to a national epidemiological measure rather than to its own case counts, which did not yet exist. Directly relevant to the blog post's claim that the on-campus line tracks policy.

headline: Staff asked not to return to campus despite the easing of restrictions
detail: UCL's response to the Prime Minister's announcement of 10 May 2020, published the following day.
quote: We are asking everyone not to return to UCL for the time being, unless you are one of our key staff who have been on-site throughout the lockdown period.
notes: A one-day lag, and the substance is divergence rather than compliance: national restrictions eased and UCL did not. The counterpart to 13 March, where UCL moved first in the other direction.

headline: Furloughed staff guaranteed against later detriment
quote: I want to be particularly clear that furloughed staff will not be subject to any disadvantage or detriment at a later date as a result of having been placed on Furlough Leave

headline: UCL furloughs staff who cannot work remotely, on full pay
detail: Following advice from the Higher Education Minister that universities should use the national scheme. UCL topped the capped government contribution up to full salary and benefits.
quote: We have now been advised by the HE Minister, Michelle Donelan, that universities should make use of the national Coronavirus Job Retention (or Furlough) scheme to cover the salaries of staff who are currently unable to work. Following this advice, we have decided to furlough staff for whom remote working is not possible.
notes: Names the minister and the advice, so the national event is identifiable and the lag computable once the ministerial statement is retrieved in stage 2.

headline: UCL-Ventura in use at 46 NHS hospitals across the UK
detail: With prototypes manufactured for testing in eleven countries.
quote: The UCL-Ventura breathing aid, a low-flow Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) device, is now being deployed to treat coronavirus patients in 46 NHS hospitals across the UK

headline: Reopening plan drawn up with UCL's own health and behaviour researchers
detail: A bespoke plan rather than a direct application of the government guidance, explicitly drawing on internal expertise.
quote: we are drawing on the expertise of our researchers, including specialists in health, education, human behaviour and infection prevention, to develop a bespoke plan that protects our community
notes: A university using its own epidemiologists to set its own policy. Relevant to the blog post's claim that the campus signal informed decisions, though the case statistics did not begin until October.

headline: UCL Covid-19 Rapid Response funding call opened
detail: Projects of six to twelve months costing £20,000 to £50,000, supported by the UCL Coronavirus Response Fund with UCLH and Moorfields NIHR Biomedical Research Centres. First deadline 2 June 2020.
quote: Applications are now invited for projects focused on rapid responses and novel solutions to understand and tackle the challenges faced during and after the coronavirus pandemic.

headline: Much of 2020-21 teaching to be remote, with face-to-face set by social distancing
detail: UCL naming Manchester and Cambridge as institutions that had already said large-group teaching would be online.
quote: we have to plan that much of our teaching will have to be delivered remotely and that the opportunities for face-to-face will be dictated to a significant extent by the social distancing constraints in place at the time
notes: The decision that shapes the whole 2020-21 year and therefore the autumn case data. Made in May for a September term, under acknowledged uncertainty.

headline: UCL signs the Wellcome Statement on Open Data
detail: With its own statement on research transparency during the pandemic.
quote: UCL has signed The Wellcome Statement on Open Data and issued its own statement to make clear our position on supporting research transparency in the context of the pandemic.

headline: Face coverings required on campus where distancing is not possible
detail: Alongside temperature checks, frequent handwashing, a one-way system and increased cleaning.
quote: we will be asking everyone on campus to wear face coverings when moving around or when social distancing is not an option, check their temperature, wash their hands frequently and use a one-way system onsite
notes: Well ahead of national requirements: face coverings became mandatory on public transport in England on 15 June 2020 and in shops on 24 July. Both national dates need retrieving in stage 2 before the comparison is stated in the rendering.

headline: Two reopening pilots named for the first weeks of June
detail: Pilot 1 from 1 June covered the Cancer Institute, Queen Square Institute of Neurology, Chemical Engineering and the Student Centre; Pilot 2 from 8 June the Main Library, Institute of Child Health, MRC LMCB and Chemistry.
quote: Pilot 1 (w/c 1 June): The Cancer Institute, Queen Square Institute of Neurology, Chemical Engineering and the Student Centre (for staff who cannot work remotely)
notes: The first named reopening of any part of the estate since the closure of 20 March, ten weeks earlier.

headline: Campus reopening pilots aligned with the dates schools were due to return
quote: we have aligned our campus reopening pilot activity with the proposed dates for schools to return, although we know that not all children will be returning
notes: A direct dependency of UCL's timetable on a national schools decision, and a clean case for the lag analysis.

headline: Face-to-face teaching to be limited to groups of about fifteen
detail: With significant parts of delivery online until a vaccine or treatment was available globally.
quote: Depending on room size, this will likely be in groups of 15 or fewer.

headline: Staff consultation launched on education principles for 2020-21
detail: Open to all staff until 1 July, feeding Education Committee on 8 June and Academic Committee and Council in June and July.
quote: Today we are launching a consultation to gather your views on what will be needed to support you and your students through Term 1 and beyond.
notes: Two documents were put out with it, the UCL Commitment to Students and Connected Learning at UCL.

headline: Term 1 plans forced early by the UCAS deadline and OfS expectations
detail: UCL stating that decisions on 2020-21 had to be taken before June so offer holders could choose.
quote: in line with comments from the Office for Students last week , we need to confirm our plans to prospective students as they decide which of their offers to accept
notes: An explicit sector-level constraint on the timing of a UCL decision. The OfS statement is a stage 2 retrieval target; reference [38] in the research document is the OfS coronavirus briefing series.

headline: UCL working with Camden and Newham on local pandemic projects
detail: Including support for autistic young Londoners, translation for the Hasidic community and free legal advice for residents.
quote: we are also having a huge impact at a local level, working with our neighbours in Camden and Newham on projects including supporting autistic young Londoners, providing translation services for the Hasidic community and offering free legal advice to residents in need
notes: The only borough-level civic work named in this period, and the local counterpart to the Camden case comparator in the data track.

headline: Keeping safe on campus guidance published
detail: Risk assessments, reduced occupancy, flexible hours to avoid peak commuting, temperature checks and face coverings.
quote: We will also be encouraging temperature checks, and asking all staff to wear a face covering when moving around campus. You can find out more, including who to contact if you have any questions, on our new Keeping safe on campus site .
notes: First appearance of a heading that recurs in 110 of the 168 newsletters, so this is the start date of the standing on-campus safety regime.

headline: Reopening pilots developed with the recognised trade unions
quote: The pilots are being carried out in line with UK Government guidance, drawing on the advice of UCL’s recognised unions and the expertise of our researchers, including specialists in health, education, human behaviour and infection prevention.

headline: UCL healthcare staff invited to the Oxford vaccine trial at UCLH
detail: Open to clinical and non-clinical healthcare staff other than office-based roles.
quote: UCL staff who have a healthcare role – for example as a member of staff at one of our partner hospitals – are invited to take part in a UCLH trial of the COVID-19 vaccine developed at the University of Oxford.
notes: The first vaccination row in the ledger, and it is a trial rather than a rollout. Vaccination proper does not reach UCL until December 2020.

headline: Schools in England begin a phased reopening
detail: The date UCL aligned its first campus reopening pilots with.
quote: Phased re-opening of schools in England
notes: UCL said on 26 May that it had aligned its pilot activity with the proposed dates for schools to return, which makes this a dependency of a UCL timetable on a national schools decision.

headline: Student Centre reopens as staff workspace, capped at 130 users
detail: Open 10.00 to 20.00 Monday to Friday for staff unable to work remotely, by pre-booking.
quote: The Student Centre will open during the week commencing Monday 1 June as a UCL staff workspace, with capacity capped at 130 users in the building 10.00–20.00, Monday–Friday.
notes: The Student Centre closed on 24 March. It reopens ten weeks later, to staff only and at a fraction of capacity.

headline: Temporary Operating Model for 2020-21 published and sent to all students
detail: Approved by Academic Committee on 29 May and communicated to current students and offer holders via Portico, with a dedicated helpline for offer holders.
quote: The Temporary Operating Model for 2020-21, setting out at a high-level how teaching will be operating next year, is available on the coronavirus information hub .
notes: The formal statement of how UCL would run the year in which the case statistics begin. Everything in the autumn 2020 data happens under this model.

headline: Oxford vaccine phase III trial to vaccinate 500 UCLH staff volunteers
detail: UCL's Vax-Hub collaboration with the Jenner Institute supplied the manufacturing platform the Oxford team adapted.
quote: Screening for the ‘phase III’ trial of the vaccine began at the end of May, and researchers plan to begin vaccinations in 500 healthy UCLH staff volunteers in June.
notes: Six months before the national rollout began. UCL's involvement in the vaccine is upstream of the vaccination programme, not part of receiving it.

headline: Student Centre entry conditional on temperature check, booking and face covering
detail: Bookable Monday to Friday, 100 people a day maximum, ID and confirmation required at reception.
quote: You will be asked to take your temperature at the entrance of the Student Centre.
notes: The daily cap tightened from the 130 announced on 26 May to 100 in practice.

headline: UCL cites ONS finding that Covid deaths are four times likelier among black adults
detail: Used to argue that the disparity could not be explained by health inequalities alone.
quote: According to the ONS, Covid-19 deaths are four times more likely among black adults than those of white ethnicity in the UK.
notes: UCL relaying an ONS finding, and it checks out: the ONS publication of 7 May 2020 gives 4.2 for Black males and 4.3 for Black females against White males and females, after adjusting for age. Now carried on the national track with the ONS wording. The ONS is explicit that adjusting for age alone does not establish cause.

headline: UCL commits to racial equality action in the context of coronavirus
detail: An institutional plan for 2020-21 covering fair admissions after exam disruption, the BAME degree awarding gap, belonging, and hardship including digital poverty.
quote: UCL’s Equality, Diversity and Inclusion team are currently working at speed on an institutional plan for 2020-21 and it will include specific action on racial equality in the context of coronavirus.
notes: Published four days after the killing of George Floyd. The newsletter connects it to the pandemic through the disproportionate mortality figures cited in the same issue.

headline: UCL works with Camden Council to make commuting possible without public transport
detail: Aimed at making cycling viable for staff returning under the pilots.
quote: we’re working with Camden Council and other local organisations to make it easier to commute to UCL without using public transport
notes: Transport is named repeatedly as the constraint on returning to campus, and here as a reason for a borough-level partnership.

headline: Face-covering guidance issued distinguishing coverings from PPE
detail: Coverings required when moving around, removable at a desk two metres from others, with PPE reserved for those who need it and exemptions acknowledged.
quote: Importantly, a face covering is a precautionary measure and not the same as personal protective equipment (PPE), which includes surgical masks and tight-fitting face masks. PPE must continue to be reserved only for those who need it.
notes: Exemptions are named explicitly for respiratory conditions and for deaf staff and those with hearing loss who rely on lip reading.

headline: Gold, Silver and Bronze structure replaced by a Crisis Leadership Team
detail: The command structure adopted in April gave way to an implementation framework once the closure and planning work was done.
quote: We now need to focus on implementing plans and have moved away from the GSB structure towards a new framework. The focus of the new framework, starting from 8 June, continues to be set by the Provost and is supported by a Crisis Leadership Team.
notes: Filed on the effective date of 8 June; announced 5 June. The second reorganisation of UCL's decision-making in three months.

headline: UCL sets policy for staff caught by the new quarantine on UK arrivals
detail: Staff abroad were told to return two weeks before they were needed and to work from home, volunteer through UCL Together, stay on furlough or take paid leave.
quote: Staff currently living abroad or wishing to travel abroad should be aware that the Government has introduced a two-week self-isolation period for anyone entering the UK on or after 8 June
notes: Filed on 8 June, the date the national rule took effect; UCL's guidance was published on 4 June, four days ahead of it. A negative lag.

headline: All library loans extended to 1 October with no late penalties
detail: Correcting a technical fault that had brought some due dates forward.
quote: All library loans are now due on 1 October or for some students, at the end of their programme of study.
notes: Extends the 5 June date set on 18 March.

headline: Provost asks for review of buildings named after eugenicists
detail: Following the recommendations of the Inquiry into the History of Eugenics at UCL, chaired by Professor Iyiola Solanke, with a recommendation due to Council on 18 June.
quote: UCL’s President & Provost Professor Michael Arthur has today formally asked the university’s ‘Buildings Naming and Renaming Committee’ immediately to start the process of reviewing the current naming of spaces and buildings after two prominent eugenicists Francis Galton and Karl Pearson.
notes: Not part of UCL's pandemic response, and included only because the pandemic newsletters were the channel that carried it. Filter on category governance if the timeline is read as a pandemic record.

headline: Face coverings become mandatory on public transport in England
detail: The Health Protection (Coronavirus, Wearing of Face Coverings on Public Transport) (England) Regulations 2020, SI 2020/592.
quote: These Regulations come into force on 15th June 2020
notes: UCL had required face coverings on campus where distancing was not possible from 22 May, twenty-four days before this. The date was carried for a while on a UCL newsletter's authority and then withdrawn, because reference 7 gives 15 June as the day non-essential shops reopened and says nothing about transport. Both are true of that day; the regulations are what establish the second.

headline: Connected Learning Essentials staff development course launched
detail: Over 800 colleagues had engaged with it within nine days.
quote: Connected Learning Essentials, UCL’s staff development course, is designed to help colleagues with the move to online and socially distant teaching. More than 800 colleagues have engaged with the course since it launched on Monday 15 June.
notes: Filed on 15 June, the launch date; reported in issue 72 of 24 June.

headline: Library Click and Collect service to open at the Main and Science Libraries
detail: Requesting, collecting, borrowing and returning books, 12.00 to 16.00 Monday to Friday.
quote: We are aiming for a ‘Click and Collect’ service to go live from Monday 15 June in the Main and Science Libraries for users to request, collect, borrow and return books.
notes: Filed on 15 June, the target date; announced 26 May. Issue 51 exists partly to correct a wrong date given in issue 50 on 22 May, which is itself a caution against trusting a single newsletter mention.

headline: Over 180 live UCL projects investigating coronavirus, almost half externally funded
quote: There are now over 180 live projects across all UCL’s faculties investigating coronavirus and its impact. Of these, almost half are externally funded.
notes: Up from the hundred reported on 15 May.

headline: Reopening widens from nine areas to about forty
detail: With line managers contacting staff individually and no compulsion to return.
quote: We are now in the third week of pilot schemes, with nine areas of UCL reopened. From today, we’re planning to restart activity in some 40 more areas of the university.
notes: The step from pilot to programme. Three months after the closure of 20 March.

headline: All staff and postgraduate researchers asked to complete a workstation assessment
detail: A display screen equipment assessment for the home working environment, with issues referred to line managers.
quote: To ensure you can work comfortably, UCL is asking all staff and postgraduate researchers to complete an online workstation assessment.
notes: Three months into remote working, which is when the temporary arrangement started being treated as a workplace.

headline: Emergency Timetabling Policy approved by the Crisis Management Team
detail: With a revised timetabling process for 2020-21 and FAQs on how the Temporary Operating Model would work in practice.
quote: An Emergency Timetabling Policy has been approved by the Crisis Management Team and our Timetabling FAQs provide some further granularity about how the Temporary Operating Model will operate in practice.
notes: The mechanism by which the Temporary Operating Model reached individual rooms and hours, which is what determined how many people were on campus in autumn 2020.

headline: Face-to-face invigilated exams ruled unlikely for 2020-21
detail: Replaced by short, timed, online and un-invigilated exams, with staff required to confirm assessment modes by 24 July for the August Module Catalogue update.
quote: It is highly likely that we will be unable to deliver face-to-face invigilated exams next year, and students need clarity about how they will be assessed.
notes: Consumer legislation is given as the reason for the July deadline, which is a legal rather than epidemiological constraint on the timing.

headline: REF2021 submission deadline reset to 31 March 2021
detail: With the impact assessment period extended to 31 December 2020 and the exercise resuming on 31 July 2020. The staff census date of 31 July 2020 was unchanged.
quote: The revised REF submission deadline is now noon on 31 March 2021 for all elements of submissions. They have also confirmed an extended assessment period for impact to 31 December 2020.
notes: Resolves the indefinite postponement announced on 25 March. A sector-level decision by the funding bodies; the primary announcement belongs on the sector track in stage 2.

headline: UCL denames the Galton and Pearson spaces
detail: Decided by the Provost and ratified by Council, with signs removed immediately.
quote: UCL has today announced it will dename spaces and buildings named after two prominent eugenicists Francis Galton and Karl Pearson.
notes: Eight days from the Provost's request to the decision. As above, contemporaneous with the pandemic rather than part of the response to it.

headline: Library Click and Collect opens at the Portico entrance
detail: Up to ten books per request, collected 12.00 to 15.00 Monday to Friday, with ID, confirmation email and a face covering required on campus.
quote: Requesting will be made available on Explore on Friday 19 June and fetching will begin next Monday, 22 June.
notes: Filed on 22 June, the date collection began. The first library service of any kind since the closure of 20 March, and it is contactless.

headline: Weekly Your Wellbeing check-in survey launched for staff and researchers
detail: Reported to the Crisis Leadership Team and to faculty level, and designed partly to test whether crisis measures were harming under-represented staff.
quote: The UCL Your Wellbeing check-in survey launches today. This short, weekly survey is the way to check in with you regularly to find out how you are coping with the coronavirus crisis and the immense amount of change that it has caused.
notes: A weekly internal measurement running alongside, and four months before, the published case statistics. The survey results are not in the archive; only the fact of their collection is.

headline: The Prime Minister announces a relaxing of the 2 metre distancing rule
detail: The move that became the "1 metre plus" guidance, taking effect with the wider easing of 4 July.
quote: PM says UK’s “national hibernation” coming to an end – announces relaxing of restrictions and 2m social distancing rule
notes: The source records a relaxing of the 2 metre rule and does not use the phrase "one metre plus"; the headline follows the source rather than UCL's wording for it. UCL kept 2 metres for Term 1 timetable planning, which is the sharpest deliberate divergence in the whole record.

headline: Fieldwork permitted to restart under Dean-approved risk assessment
detail: Conditional on voluntary participation, the reopening plans, and UK and destination travel rules. International travel on UCL business remained barred until 1 August.
quote: Fieldwork can restart from this week, as long as individuals wish to take part

headline: UCL passes £1m raised for its pandemic response
detail: Directed at research on tracking, treating and preventing the virus, at societal recovery, and at student hardship.
quote: UCL has raised over £1m to drive the university’s response to the pandemic, through generous donations from our supporters, alumni and friends.

headline: Virus Watch launched with 42,500 participants
detail: Regular symptom surveys, a movement-tracking app, and blood tests and swabs for 10,000 participants, intended to inform government and NHS planning.
quote: This week UCL launched Virus Watch, one of the largest and most comprehensive studies of COVID-19 in the UK, with 42,500 people taking part to help us learn more about the next phase of the pandemic.
notes: UCL running national community surveillance while having no case data of its own. Its own counting begins 12 October 2020.

headline: Undergraduate bursaries increased for 2020-21
detail: The lowest income band rose from £2,500 to £3,350, with uplifts across all four bands, applied automatically and extended to students who joined from 2017-18.
quote: UCL is increasing the amount of financial support available as part of our Undergraduate Bursary for the academic year 2020/21.
notes: Categorised accommodation as the nearest available slot for student financial support; the category list has no hardship or finance value.

headline: The first local lockdown is announced for Leicester
detail: Announced by the Secretary of State for Health and Social Care.
quote: Matt Hancock announces that the UK’s first local lockdown would be applied in Leicester and parts of Leicestershire
notes: UCL cited this on 8 July as a reason for caution in its own planning.

headline: Government research support package announced in two parts
detail: A COVID-19 Grant Extension Allocation to sustain UKRI and National Academies awards to September 2021, and a Research Stabilisation Package of low-interest loans with some grants.
quote: At the end of last month, the UK Government announced a support package for research, made up of two elements.
notes: Dated to June 2020 with month precision, because the newsletter says only 'at the end of last month'. Day precision would assert more than the source supports. The primary announcement is a stage 2 retrieval target and the row should be re-dated to day precision once it is found.

headline: Staff allowed onto campus by rota to collect belongings
detail: Buildings opened on set dates in morning or afternoon slots, by request through Faculty Directors of Operations or Security.
quote: From tomorrow, Wednesday 1 July, it will be possible to collect personal belongings from campus on a pre-arranged, rota basis.
notes: Filed on 1 July, the effective date; announced 30 June.

headline: The first local lockdown comes into force in Leicester
detail: The same day as the wider easing in the rest of England.
quote: UK’s first local lockdown comes into force in Leicester and parts of Leicestershire. More restrictions are eased in England, including reopening of pubs, restaurants, hairdressers.
notes: The two limbs of this entry are why 4 July is the phase boundary in this chronology: England eased and one city did not.

headline: Taught postgraduates given access to Student Centre and Click and Collect
detail: For students unable to study remotely, by advance booking, with distancing and face coverings in force.
quote: From Monday 6 July taught postgraduate students who are unable to study remotely may use the pilot Student Centre learning spaces and the Click & Collect service for the Main and Science Libraries
notes: The first return of any students to campus since March, and it is limited to those who cannot work at home.

headline: UCL signs the London Higher COVID-19 Secure Charter
detail: Ten principles for a safe return to campus, adopted by more than twenty London institutions.
quote: London Higher has today published their COVID-19 Secure Charter. The charter sets out ten key principles that member institutions are working on to ensure a safe return to campus for students across London this autumn.
notes: A sector-level commitment with a named document. London Higher is a stage 2 retrieval target for the sector track.

headline: Wellbeing survey results reviewed weekly by the Provost and Crisis Leadership Team
quote: The Provost and Crisis Leadership Team review these results in person every week. They form a central part of their decision-making process
notes: Establishes that a weekly internal data feed was already part of decision-making before the case statistics existed. Relevant to how the October 2020 case page was used.

headline: Digital first recommended for Term 1, with local teams deciding specifics
detail: A mix of asynchronous and synchronous learning with some campus-based, laboratory and studio teaching, and decisions devolved to programme teams.
quote: In Term 1, UCL recommends a ‘digital first’ approach (a mixture of asynchronous and synchronous learning), with some campus-based face-to-face as well as lab- and studio/practice-based teaching activity for students, led by academic or teaching staff.
notes: Names Tier 4 visa requirements and the implications of wholly online programmes as planning considerations, which is an immigration constraint on teaching mode.

headline: Four additional closure days added, extending the Christmas break to two weeks
detail: Friday 28 August before the bank holiday, and 21 to 23 December, closing UCL from 18 December 2020 to 4 January 2021.
quote: UCL will be closed from 5:30pm on Friday 18 December 2020 until 9am on Monday 4 January 2021.
notes: Decided in July. The closure period turned out to coincide with the Alpha wave and the second national lockdown, and with the highest weekly case count in the whole UCL series.

headline: Roadmap for returning to campus published, targeting 25% of staff on site
detail: Setting out which buildings would reopen and when, while most staff continued to work from home.
quote: we are also beginning to work towards a return to something approaching normality, with the launch today of our roadmap for returning to campus . This sets out the plan and supporting guidance for reopening buildings gradually and safely, so that around 25% of staff can be back on site at any one time.
notes: The 25% ceiling is the planning assumption behind the autumn 2020 campus population, and therefore behind the on-campus case counts when they begin in October.

headline: Temperature checks extended from the Student Centre across campus
detail: Alongside handwashing, distancing, additional cleaning, face coverings and PPE where appropriate.
quote: trialling temperature checks at the Student Centre, which we’re now rolling out across campus
notes: Temperature screening was later widely judged ineffective for COVID-19. Recorded as what UCL did, not as a measure that worked.

headline: UCL cites the Leicester local lockdown as a reason for caution
quote: The local lockdown announced in Leicester last week, and the possibility of lockdowns in some London boroughs, show us that we cannot yet take our safety for granted.
notes: An explicit reference to a national event shaping a UCL decision. The Leicester lockdown of 29 June 2020 is a stage 2 retrieval target.

headline: UCL joins the Hidden Disabilities Sunflower scheme
detail: So that staff with non-visible disabilities could signal a need for help while returning to campus.
quote: UCL has recently signed up to the Hidden Disabilities Sunflower scheme , which allows colleagues to discreetly signal to others that they may need additional help

headline: UCL keeps 2 metre distancing after the government moves to one metre plus
detail: Justified by reference to the Chief Medical Officer's advice and PHE guidance, and by the need for flexibility if guidance changed or a second wave came.
quote: although the government has announced its “1 metre plus” approach to social distancing, we have confirmed that we will continue to use a 2 metre guideline for timetable planning for Term 1
notes: The clearest deliberate divergence from national policy in the record, and in the cautious direction. It set the room capacities for the whole of Term 1 and so directly shaped how many people were on campus in autumn 2020.

headline: Face coverings made mandatory on campus for staff, students and visitors
detail: Required when moving between or around buildings and wherever 2 metres could not be maintained, with a published exemptions policy and Sunflower lanyards for invisible disabilities.
quote: Face coverings must be worn by all staff, students and visitors on campus when walking between or around buildings and where it is not possible to maintain 2 metre social distancing from others.
notes: Fourteen days before face coverings became mandatory in English shops on 24 July 2020, and framed as protecting others from an asymptomatic wearer rather than protecting the wearer.

headline: Bloomsbury Café reopens as the first Students' Union outlet on campus
detail: Monday to Friday, 11.00 to 15.00, with other outlets to follow in September.
quote: Students’ Union UCL are beginning to reopen their outlets and commercial spaces on campus, starting with the Bloomsbury Café which reopened earlier this week.
notes: Week precision: issue 89 of 17 July says only 'earlier this week', so the exact day is not established. Filed at the start of that week.

headline: Advisory report models an Rt of 1.7 from September as its worst-case scenario
detail: "Preparing for a challenging winter 2020/21", produced at the request of the Government Chief Scientific Adviser.
quote: The model assumes that Rt rises to 1.7 from September 2020
notes: UCL relayed this on 16 July 2020 and stage 1 flagged the Rt figure as not to be repeated until checked. It checks out, with a distinction worth keeping: 1.7 is an assumption the model was run under to explore a reasonable worst case, not a forecast of what Rt would be. Reporting it as a prediction would misstate what the report did.

headline: Council postpones performance-related pay for grade 10 staff to August 2021
detail: Framed as intergenerational fairness, with staff at lower grades unaffected.
quote: we have taken the difficult decision to postpone any performance-related pay awards for grade 10 staff until August 2021
notes: One of three payroll measures confirmed by Council on 14 July, and the only one that is not voluntary.

headline: Voluntary Retirement Scheme opened for staff aged 66 and over
detail: Open until 31 October 2020, with eligibility set at age 66 on 1 October 2020, alongside voluntary unpaid leave, career breaks and temporary part-time working.
quote: Later this month we will also launch a Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS) for staff aged 66 and over.
notes: Explicitly to preserve the jobs of staff earlier in their careers. UCL still had not made compulsory redundancies at this point.

headline: Travel ban partially lifted for the Common Travel Area and FCO-exempted countries
detail: Only essential travel permitted elsewhere until 1 October 2020, and all international travel to be booked through Key Travel.
quote: Travel on UCL business is now permitted within the CTA or to FCO exempted countries. Until 1 October 2020 only essential travel outside this area is permitted.
notes: Follows the FCO relaxing its advice the previous week. The first loosening of the travel restriction imposed on 11 March 2020, four months earlier.

headline: Advisory report warns of an Rt of 1.7 from September as a reasonable worst case
detail: 'Preparing for a challenging winter 2020/21', produced by 37 experts including UCL academics at the request of the Government Chief Scientific Adviser.
quote: ‘Preparing for a challenging winter 2020/21’ has found there is a high degree of uncertainty about how the pandemic will evolve in the UK over the coming months, but suggests we should prepare for a ‘reasonable worst-case scenario’ where the average number of people that one infected person will pass the virus on to (Rt value) rises to 1.7 from September 2020 onwards.
notes: UCL relaying a report its own academics contributed to, and it checks out against the Academy of Medical Sciences report itself. One distinction the newsletter loses: 1.7 is an assumption the model was run under to explore a reasonable worst case, not a forecast. The warning is issued two months before the autumn term and the surge that followed it.

headline: Recruitment freeze partially relaxed where student numbers exceed forecast
detail: A phased relaxation for some academic and professional services posts, with the freeze otherwise still in force and internal sourcing required first.
quote: In the light of our latest student number projections, we can start a phased and controlled relaxation of the recruitment freeze for some academic and professional services posts in Schools where student numbers look likely to exceed previous forecasts.
notes: The first sign that the feared collapse in student numbers was not materialising. It reverses part of the emergency measure of 24 April.

headline: Term 1 room allocations issued under social distancing, with a 10 August timetable deadline
detail: Departments required to enter all online and on-site synchronous activity into CMIS.
quote: This week colleagues will be contacted with information about departmental room allocations for Term 1, in line with social distancing guidelines.
notes: The point at which the 2 metre decision of 8 July becomes a concrete allocation of rooms, and therefore the mechanism setting autumn campus occupancy.

headline: Eugenics inquiry group to report an implementation plan by December
detail: With a second working group set up on the recommendations from the staff and student Town Hall on Race, also reporting before the end of the year.
quote: The group looking at the recommendations from the Inquiry met for the first time this week, and will produce an implementation plan by December.
notes: As with the denaming rows, this is contemporaneous with the pandemic rather than part of the response to it, and is filed under governance so it can be filtered out.

headline: UCL funds local pandemic projects in Newham, one of the worst-affected boroughs
detail: Small grants to projects co-developed with local groups, support for artists and researchers in the Olympic boroughs, and work with east London schools.
quote: Throughout the pandemic we have remained committed to being a good neighbour to communities in east London, especially in Newham, which is sadly one of the boroughs most affected by COVID-19.
notes: The second borough-level civic strand after Camden. UCL's claim about Newham's standing is not evidenced in the newsletter and should not be repeated without checking.

headline: UCL notes face coverings becoming mandatory in English shops
detail: UCL convened a group with its own experts and Students' Union leaders to consider whether to extend campus requirements further.
quote: Since then, the Government’s guidance has changed and face coverings will now be mandatory in shops and supermarkets from 24 July.
notes: Filed on 24 July, the national effective date; reported by UCL on 15 July. UCL's own campus mandate had come into force on 10 July, ahead of it. The national date is a stage 2 retrieval target.

headline: Individual Risk Assessments offered to staff worried about returning
detail: With the explicit possibility that the outcome is not returning to campus at this stage.
quote: You may be asked to complete an Individual Risk Assessment to help understand your concerns and identify any measures that might manage any risks to your health and take into account your circumstances. In some cases that may mean that you do not return to campus at this stage.

headline: Staff who can work remotely may do so until January 2021
detail: With an option to work on campus from 1 September when most buildings opened, subject to the 25% occupancy cap.
quote: If your role means you don’t need to attend site to do your work , you may be able to continue working remotely until January 2021, when this policy will be reviewed.
notes: The policy under which the whole of autumn 2020 was run, and therefore the policy behind the on-campus case counts when the series begins on 12 October.

headline: UCL installs 600 cycle racks in response to commuting fears in the wellbeing survey
detail: With a cycling buddy scheme, the tax-free cycle scheme, and advice on off-peak travel and part-journey walking.
quote: Many of you have let us know through the Your Wellbeing survey that commuting to work is an area of concern.
notes: A traceable line from an internal data collection to a physical change on campus, which is the pattern the case statistics later followed.

headline: UKRI allocates UCL £10.8m to sustain grant-funded research
detail: About 6% of UCL's UKRI award portfolio, prioritising projects ending before 31 March 2021 and those with staff who had been furloughed.
quote: UCL has been allocated £10.8m, which is equivalent to about 6% of our current UKRI award portfolio.
notes: The concrete outcome of the government research support package recorded in June. UKRI also asked that the money mitigate disadvantage to protected groups.

headline: Provost takes a 20% pay reduction donated to the student hardship fund
detail: For six months from 1 August 2020, alongside a Give as You Earn scheme opened for the Senior Management Team.
quote: I have volunteered to take a pay reduction of 20% of my salary, which will be donated to the student hardship fund, for six months from August 1st.
notes: Filed on the effective date of 1 August 2020; announced 24 April in issue 31.

headline: Newsletter cadence drops from daily to twice weekly at issue 100
