detail: Mondays and Wednesdays, in response to a reader survey asking for fewer emails.
quote: With that in mind, from today you’ll receive an update twice a week on Mondays and Wednesdays.
notes: The first cadence change in the series. It thins again to weekly on 12 October 2020 and to roughly monthly through 2022, so the frequency of the newsletters is itself a record of how urgent the situation felt.

headline: Staff quarantining after non-essential travel must use leave, not paid absence
detail: Prompted by the Foreign Office revoking Spain's travel corridor at short notice on 27 July, and Luxembourg soon after.
quote: From 3 August, where travel is not for agreed essential UCL work, the default position is for the member of staff to work remotely during their period of self-isolation if possible, by agreement with your line manager. If that is not possible, you should take any remaining annual leave entitlement followed by unpaid leave.
notes: A tightening. In June, staff caught by quarantine were offered paid leave as a fallback; from August the fallback is unpaid.

headline: UCL reports shutting over 200 buildings and delivering 647 online exams
detail: A hundred-working-day retrospective, also recording 147 student interns appointed to move teaching materials online.
quote: Colleagues from every Faculty, Vice Provost’s Office and Professional Services department have, at speed, first shut down over 200 buildings on campus
notes: UCL's own summary of the first phase, and the source of the 647 online exams figure. Both numbers are UCL's own and are not independently checkable from the archive.

headline: No Detriment Principle for Staff published, covering promotions and appraisals
detail: UCL estimated around 40% of employees had been caring for children or loved ones during the pandemic.
quote: UCL leadership have therefore set out clearly how we are going to ensure that all this is taken into account in our No Detriment Principle for Staff .
notes: The staff counterpart to the student no-detriment principle adopted on 7 April 2020, four months earlier.

headline: UCL undertakes not to reuse teaching recordings without the originator's consent
detail: Setting aside the position in the Intellectual Property Policy, which assigns film and sound recordings to UCL, for the 2019-20 and 2020-21 academic years.
quote: UCL has committed, notwithstanding the position in the UCL Intellectual Property Policy, not to use teaching-related film and sound recordings created during academic years 2019/20 and 2020/21 without the originators’ consent
notes: A staff concern created directly by the move online: recording lectures turned teaching into an asset the policy already claimed.

headline: Face covering policy widened to inside offices, labs and teaching spaces
detail: Strongly encouraged throughout campus and mandatory within two metres of another person, with clear-panel coverings procured centrally for classroom teaching.
quote: Face coverings are now strongly encouraged when you’re on campus, both inside buildings and when moving around campus. This includes in offices, labs and teaching spaces.
notes: The third tightening in two months: 22 May when distancing was impossible, 10 July mandatory when moving around, 12 August extended indoors throughout.

headline: Protecting Time for Work recommendations issued in response to workload data
detail: Meetings in core hours, hour-long meetings cut to 50 minutes, and email and meeting efficiency measures.
quote: Our weekly Your Wellbeing survey continues to highlight that many of you are struggling with your workloads.
notes: A second traceable line from the weekly survey to a policy change, after the cycle racks in July.

headline: All Term One core teaching to be online, with 1 to 2 hours a week face to face
detail: Students free to study on campus or from anywhere in the world, and to change their mind mid-term without penalty.
quote: We’re currently anticipating a maximum of 1-2 hours a week of face to face teaching time, although this will vary depending on programme.
notes: The most concrete statement of how much on-campus contact autumn 2020 actually involved, and essential context for reading the on-campus case counts that begin in October.

headline: UCL accepts all students meeting their original offer after the A level U-turn
detail: Following the government's decision to use teacher-predicted grades rather than the Ofqual algorithm.
quote: We are delighted to accept all students who meet the terms of their original offer.
notes: The decision that produced the exceptionally large first-year intake, which UCL names on 26 August as one cause of the study-space shortage. It is therefore upstream of how crowded campus was in autumn 2020.

headline: Campus Opening Guide sets out a four-stage building reopening process
detail: Planning, building preparation, approval to open and confirmation, with each department nominating a liaison to the Estates team.
quote: Each department must nominate a dedicated person to liaise with the Estates Team throughout the building reopening process.
notes: The procedure by which all campus buildings were open by 2 September 2020.

headline: Fieldwork framework published to govern planning, approval and management
detail: Working alongside existing risk assessments, with pre-conditions and a checklist before approval, overseen by a dedicated group.
quote: A framework has been developed which informs the planning, approval and management of fieldwork and works alongside the existing risk assessments.
notes: Formalises the fieldwork restart permitted on 25 June 2020. Added after a coverage check flagged issue 105 as decision-bearing but uncited.

headline: Visitors to campus must declare symptoms and register where they went
detail: Contact details and areas visited collected so UCL could respond to cases.
quote: They will also be asked to supply their contact details and the areas of campus they are visiting. We will use this information to make sure campus is as safe as possible and respond to any potential cases of COVID-19 should they occur.
notes: UCL building its own contact-tracing capability three weeks before the case reporting tool was announced.

headline: Staff offices released to students as study space after distancing cuts capacity
detail: Floors in Bidborough House and Torrington Place given over to students, against the 6,000 study spaces available the previous year.
quote: Social distancing put in place to ensure the safety of everyone on campus means that the number of student study spaces on campus will be much reduced compared with the 6,000 we had last year.
notes: Names three compounding causes: distancing, growth in postgraduate applications, and the large first-year intake following the A level U-turn. A direct consequence of the 2 metre decision of 8 July.

headline: Presumption of return from 1 September for staff whose work requires the site
detail: Covering face-to-face teaching, some professional services and technical services in laboratories.
quote: If you need to be onsite to do your job (e.g. to deliver face to face teaching, some Professional Services support or technical services in a laboratory), then there is a presumption that you will return to campus for the number of hours required in order to fulfil your role from 1 September.
notes: Filed on 1 September, the effective date; announced 27 July. The two limbs of this policy — presumption to return for some, remote until January for others — are what the on-campus and off-campus split in the case data is measuring.

headline: All campus buildings open on schedule for the new academic year
detail: Over 100 buildings requiring safety and statutory checks, completed to the July roadmap.
quote: With thanks to the Estates Operations team and colleagues across UCL, all buildings on campus are now open, on schedule and in time for the start of the new term.
notes: Five and a half months after the closure of 20 March 2020. Open, but under the 25% occupancy cap and 2 metre distancing.

headline: Pre-enrolment data used to forecast how many students would be on campus
quote: It is particularly urgent this year, as we will use this to forecast student numbers on campus and manage activities within our 2-metre social distancing guidelines.
notes: UCL predicting campus occupancy from enrolment before it could measure it. The case statistics that began six weeks later gave it a measurement instead.

headline: Zoom licensed for a year because it was the most reliable platform for China
detail: Supported by ISD from 2 September alongside Blackboard Collaborate and Microsoft Teams.
quote: UCL has purchased a 12-month licence for Zoom, as it is currently the most reliable platform for access from China.
notes: A platform decision driven by where students physically were. Many were expected to study the whole of Term 1 from outside the UK.

headline: Student Success Advisers appointed, one for every 200 undergraduates
detail: Embedded in academic departments and contacting students before and after arrival.
quote: Each Adviser will be responsible for around 200 students, acting as their first point of contact for any questions or problems they may have, and proactively contacting them before and after they arrive.

headline: Student Support Fund opened for students facing severe financial hardship
detail: Prioritising students from low-income families and BAME backgrounds, disabled students and those with experience of care or homelessness, and receiving the Provost's donated salary.
quote: We know that many students are experiencing severe financial hardship this year. The situation for some is so critical that they are being forced to consider leaving UCL.
notes: The destination of the 20% salary reduction announced on 24 April, now opened to staff donations.

headline: No national pay uplift for 2020-21; UCL raises London weighting by 2%
detail: National negotiations agreed no uplift because of the sector's financial position. UCL kept automatic incremental progression on grades 1 to 9 and backdated the London weighting rise to 1 August.
quote: UCL, like most universities in the UK, takes part in national pay negotiations where it was agreed there would be no pay uplift for 2020–21, due to the financial impact of COVID-19 on the sector nationally.
notes: A sector-level decision by UCEA that UCL partly offset locally. The UCEA settlement is a stage 2 retrieval target for the sector track.

headline: Provost notes the national daily case count clearly rising again
detail: Written the week the rule of six was introduced and three weeks before term began.
quote: with the daily national number of new cases clearly on the rise again, it remains a time of great uncertainty
notes: UCL watching national figures because it had none of its own. The reporting tool announced in the same issue is the answer to exactly this.

headline: UCL announces a reporting tool to monitor and respond to cases at UCL
detail: Due mid-September, designed with UCL public health experts who had been advising the government.
quote: This guidance will remain in place until mid-September, when we will launch a new reporting tool to monitor and respond to coronavirus cases at UCL. This system is being designed with UCL public health experts who have been advising the Government.
notes: The origin of the dataset this archive preserves. The published case page first appears in the archive on 12 October 2020, about a month after this announcement, and the first published figure is dated 2020-10-09. This row is the single most important link between the newsletter track and the data track.

headline: The rule of six bans social gatherings above six in England
detail: Applied indoors and outdoors.
quote: ‘Rule of six’ – indoor and outdoor social gatherings above six banned in England
notes: UCL noted it on 9 September while saying it had not yet decided what to do, which is rare candour in the record.

headline: Quality assurance processes temporarily relaxed to cut administrative workload
detail: Internal Quality Review deferred a year for most departments, extenuating circumstances reporting suspended, the emergency module amendment procedure continued, and peer observation reporting suspended.
quote: A series of temporary modifications to quality assurance processes at departmental level has been agreed for 2020-21, to uphold UCL’s academic standards while reducing administrative workload.

headline: Rule of six noted as UCL considers its response
quote: the Government has reported a rise in coronavirus cases and limited social gatherings to six people from Monday. UCL is monitoring the situation and considering our response.
notes: Filed on 14 September, the Monday the national limit took effect; reported by UCL on 9 September. A rare case of UCL saying openly that it had not yet decided what to do.

headline: Asymptomatic testing ruled out as a routine offer
quote: Testing of asymptomatic staff or students will only be undertaken where our public health advisers consider this appropriate, and will not be offered routinely.
notes: Load-bearing for reading the case data. The published counts are confirmed cases arising largely from symptomatic testing, so they undercount by design and the size of the undercount is unknown.

headline: UCL to provide up to 1,000 tests a day for symptomatic staff and students
detail: Built on an August pilot in the Paul O'Gorman Building, complementing rather than replacing national testing, with positives referred to NHS Test and Trace.
quote: We will provide up to 1,000 tests every day for symptomatic staff and students across UCL by the start of term.
notes: Prompted by the widely reported failure of NHS testing capacity in September 2020. UCL built its own because the national system could not be relied on.

headline: UCL to work with Camden and Islington public health teams on case response
quote: We will, of course, continue to work with Camden and Islington public health teams and with the London Coronavirus Response Cell.
notes: Names Camden explicitly as a public health partner, which is the institutional counterpart to the Camden case comparator in the data track.

headline: Connect to Protect reporting tool launched for staff and students
detail: Collecting symptoms, testing status, self-isolation status and areas of campus recently visited, to monitor the number and location of potential cases.
quote: When you log-in, you will be asked about any symptoms you have, if you are being tested for coronavirus, if you are self-isolating, and if you have visited any areas of campus recently. We will use this information to monitor the number and location of any potential coronavirus cases, and take action where necessary to keep our campus as safe as possible.
notes: Filed on 17 September, the day issue 112 said the tool would be available; the description here is from issue 113 of 21 September. This is the collection mechanism behind the published case counts.

headline: Scenario plans published for positive cases and further lockdowns
detail: Including criteria for closing buildings, additional cleaning, and how people at risk would be notified.
quote: Colleagues across UCL have also completed detailed planning in case any students or members of staff test positive for coronavirus, or if further lockdown restrictions are introduced by Government.

headline: Face coverings extended to UCL's outdoor spaces
detail: Expected everywhere on campus and mandatory within two metres of another person.
quote: All staff, students and visitors are expected to wear face coverings, if they can, when on campus, both inside buildings and when moving around UCL's outdoor spaces;
notes: The fourth and widest version of the policy, five days before term began.

headline: NHS COVID-19 contact tracing app launched and promoted to UCL staff
detail: Recommended alongside, not instead of, reporting symptoms through Connect to Protect.
quote: The NHS has launched a new contact tracing app, which notifies individuals if they have been in significant proximity with anyone who later tests positive for coronavirus, without personal data leaving your smartphone.
notes: Filed on 24 September, the national launch date of the app in England and Wales; reported by UCL on 28 September. The national date needs confirming against a primary source in stage 2.

headline: Community Commitment to Protect Each Other issued with the Students' Union
detail: Setting expectations on respecting others, reporting sickness and safety on campus and beyond, sent to all students on the first day of term.
quote: Central to this is the newly developed Community Commitment to Protect Each Other . This outlines what is expected of everyone – staff and students alike – with expectations about respecting and protecting each other, reporting sickness and keeping safe on campus and in the wider community.
notes: Issued alongside student disciplinary guidance for breaches of safety requirements, so the commitment was backed by sanction.

headline: Free seasonal flu vaccination vouchers offered to all UK staff
detail: In partnership with Boots, framed as reducing the burden of respiratory disease on the NHS.
quote: UCL is supporting a seasonal flu vaccination programme for all staff in the UK during the Autumn Term in partnership with Boots Pharmacies.
notes: The only vaccination UCL could offer in autumn 2020. COVID-19 vaccination did not begin nationally until 8 December 2020.

headline: RegisterUCL attendance system introduced to meet public health requirements
quote: The Registrar has written to Faculty Tutors and DOOs explaining how attendance must be captured in the coming year to ensure we are complying with Public Health England’s regulations to keep our campus safe.
notes: A second presence-recording system alongside Connect to Protect. Neither is the same as the on-campus marker in the published case data, which records a visit of 15 minutes or more in the two days before symptoms or test.

headline: Term 1 begins on 28 September, coinciding with Yom Kippur
detail: Departments asked to be flexible about start-of-term requirements for Jewish students observing the fast.
quote: Yom Kippur this year coincides with the first day of term on Monday 28 September, and we would like to encourage all departments to be flexible about start of term requirements and activities
notes: Establishes the first day of Term 1 as 28 September 2020, which is the reference point for reading the October case surge. The published case series begins eleven days later.

headline: China Connect launched to give students in China reliable access to teaching
detail: Routing connections from mainland China to London via Shanghai.
quote: This week ISD launched a new service, China Connect, to ensure students in China have reliable and consistent access to the resources they need to support their teaching and learning activities.
notes: By 6 October over 2,800 users were on it, which is a measure of how many students were studying Term 1 from outside the UK and therefore absent from the campus case counts.

headline: Busiest online teaching day so far, with 166,000 Moodle visits
detail: Nearly 59,000 Moodle users, over 2,800 Zoom sessions and 763 Blackboard Collaborate sessions in one day, with nearly 250 virtual common rooms set up.
quote: 5 October was the busiest online day so far, with nearly 59,000 Moodle users logging over 166,000 visits on this day alone.
notes: A measure of how much of teaching was happening off campus in the week the case counting began.

headline: Crisis structure stood down and a Public Health Advisory Panel created
detail: Normal management resumed, with a new expert panel chaired by Professor Graham Hart, Dean of Population Health Sciences, to inform planning and coordinate public health activity.
quote: The Provost has taken the decision to stand down UCL’s crisis structure and revert to the university’s normal ways of working, with the Senior Management Team continuing to function as an advisory body for the Provost.
notes: The third and final reorganisation: mitigation group in March, Gold/Silver/Bronze in April, Crisis Leadership Team in June, and now back to normal with a standing public health panel. It happens one week before the case page goes live and four weeks before the second national lockdown.

headline: UCL antigen testing facility begins issuing home self-test kits
detail: For symptomatic students in UCL halls and symptomatic staff whose role required them on campus.
quote: UCL has established a COVID-19 antigen testing facility, which is providing home self-test kits to symptomatic students based in UCL halls and symptomatic staff whose role requires them to work on campus.
notes: Narrower in practice than the 1,000 tests a day for all symptomatic staff and students announced on 16 September. Eligibility is restricted to hall residents and on-site staff.

headline: UCL begins publishing daily confirmed case counts
detail: First row of the published series. 336 readings follow, to 2022-05-11.
notes: The case page was announced in issue 110 of 9 September 2020 and described in issue 119 of 12 October 2020, but the first published figure is dated 2020-10-09. Figures were published each weekday morning correct to 5pm the previous day, with weekend figures folded into Tuesday, so a Tuesday reading covers Saturday to Monday.

headline: Case definition set as positive tests reported to the Public Health Daily Review Group
quote: New cases are defined as new confirmed positive test results reported to UCL’s Public Health Daily Review Group.
notes: The definition behind every number in the dataset. A case had to be tested, confirmed, and reported to UCL to be counted, which is three separate opportunities for undercounting.

headline: Case page updated weekday mornings, correct to 5pm the previous day
detail: Weekend figures folded into Tuesday's report.
quote: These data will be updated by 9am Monday to Friday. Figures are correct as of 5pm the previous day. Figures received over the weekend will be included in Tuesday’s report.
notes: The primary source for two conventions the archive documents: that Tuesday's figure covers Saturday to Monday, and that each figure lags reality by up to a day. Both must be carried into any reading of the daily series.

headline: Newsletter cadence drops from twice weekly to weekly on Mondays
quote: To reduce the pressure on your inboxes a little bit, you will now receive a coronavirus update once a week on Monday afternoons.
notes: The second cadence change, in the same issue that launches the case page. From this point the newsletters thin while the data thickens.

headline: UCL publishes a webpage of confirmed COVID-19 cases among staff and students
detail: Showing cases in the last 24 hours, the last 7 days, and the total since Term 1 began on 28 September.
quote: UCL has published a webpage showing the numbers of confirmed cases of COVID-19 among UCL’s staff and students.
notes: The page this whole archive exists to preserve. Announced on 9 September, launched here. The first published figure in covid_raw.csv is dated 2020-10-09, three days before this newsletter, so the page existed briefly before it was announced.

headline: A three-tier system of restrictions starts in England
detail: London moved to Tier 2 on 17 October and UCL stayed open.
quote: A new three-tier system of Covid-19 restrictions starts in England
notes: The tier system is the mechanism by which national policy reached UCL geographically rather than sectorally.

headline: London moves to Tier 2 and campus stays open
detail: Indoor socialising outside the household banned, rule of six outdoors, no travel to Tier 3 areas. For students in halls, the household is everyone sharing a kitchen or bathroom.
quote: London has moved to a Tier 2 (high) alert level for COVID-19 and additional restrictions have been introduced to help reduce the spread of infection. Many of the restrictions are the same as before and campus remains open, with measures in place to keep everyone as safe as possible.
notes: Filed on 17 October, when London entered Tier 2; reported by UCL on 19 October, a two-day lag. Face-to-face teaching continued unchanged, which is a decision as much as the tiering was.

headline: Cases found most frequently in student accommodation
detail: With a contact defined as close proximity from two days before symptoms to ten days after onset.
quote: As we find cases of COVID-19 across UCL (most frequently in our student accommodation) the team will work with each case to understand who is a ‘contact’ and needs to self-isolate.
notes: Directly relevant to reading the on-campus marker. If transmission was concentrated in halls rather than in teaching spaces, the on-campus flag records where people had been, not where they were infected — which is exactly what the archive documentation says it means.

headline: Monthly building safety inspections made mandatory
detail: Approved by the Health and Safety Committee, with 30 departmental inspections across 25 buildings done and Safety Services having visited 58 buildings and 197 teaching spaces.
quote: UCL’s Health and Safety Committee has approved a mandatory safety monitoring programme, to ensure compliance with existing implemented COVID-19 risk control measures which began in August.

headline: UCL case management described as its own version of contact tracing
detail: Run in partnership with Camden and Islington Public Health and linked to the national test and trace programme.
quote: This response includes case management, which is our version of ‘tracing’, and our internal testing provision, both of which are linked into the national ‘test and trace’ programme.
notes: UCL running a parallel local system to the national one. The published counts come from this system, not from NHS Test and Trace.

headline: Terms 2 and 3 expected to run like Term 1
detail: Core teaching and assessment online with limited on-campus activity, communicated to students jointly with Students' Union officers.
quote: indicating it is likely that teaching in Terms Two and Three will be similar to Term One; all core teaching and assessment online, and a limited amount of educational activity on campus, with alternative activity for students not on campus
notes: Signalled a week before the second national lockdown was announced, and formalised on 9 November.

headline: The Prime Minister announces a second national lockdown for England
detail: Announced on a Saturday; the measures came into force on 5 November.
quote: PM announces a second lockdown in England to prevent a “medical and moral disaster” for the NHS
notes: This source does not say that universities were to stay open. That is UCL's account of the policy, recorded in the UCL row of 1 November, and it still needs a primary source of its own. The distinction matters because the exemption is the reason the case series behaves differently in the two lockdowns.

headline: Provost notes universities were meant to stay open this time
quote: One of the main differences between this lockdown and the first earlier this year is the intention for schools, colleges and universities to remain open.
notes: The single sentence that explains why the UCL case series behaves so differently in the two lockdowns. Needs a primary source for the government policy in stage 2.

headline: UCL to remain open through the second national lockdown
detail: The Provost's response to the announcement of 31 October, keeping libraries, study spaces, halls, catering and laboratories open, with face-to-face teaching under review.
quote: UCL will remain open, continuing to operate in a COVID-secure way.
notes: A one-day lag on the announcement of Saturday 31 October, and the sharpest contrast with March 2020: the first lockdown closed UCL, the second did not, because government policy this time was for universities to stay open. Files 122 and 124 are the same message duplicated in the archive; only 122 is cited.

headline: Newsletter frequency increased again in response to the second lockdown
quote: We will increase the frequency of these Coronavirus update emails to give you the information you need as soon as possible.
notes: The only time in the record the cadence goes up rather than down, which makes the newsletter frequency a usable proxy for institutional alarm. Note this newsletter is dated 2 November in its body; UCL's index page titles it 3 November and is wrong.

headline: The second national lockdown comes into force in England
detail: A four-week closure of non-essential retail, with educational settings treated differently from the first lockdown.
quote: Second national lockdown comes into force in England

headline: COVID-19 Career Support Scheme opened for staff whose careers were set back
detail: Part of the Equity and Inclusion Plan 2020-21, funding things such as additional childcare or salary costs.
quote: this scheme invites staff whose careers are at risk of being negatively affected by the pandemic due to equity and inclusion-related circumstances to apply for support or funding to help mitigate this impact

headline: Temporary operating model for Terms 2 and 3 published
detail: Fundamentally the same as Term 1, with the flexibility to increase or decrease on-campus activity according to national, regional and local rules.
quote: The operating model for the rest of this academic year will fundamentally be the same as in Term 1 and will have the flexibility either to increase or decrease the face-to-face activity, teaching and learning, and research and innovation on campus based on the national, regional and local regulations and guidance.
notes: An explicit statement that campus activity was indexed to external regulation rather than to UCL's own case counts. This is the mechanism the blog post's central claim depends on.

headline: Travel restricted to essential journeys only until 2 December
detail: With UCL's insurance cover reduced to a £50,000 limit for COVID-related changes and flexible tickets required.
quote: In line with the latest guidance from the UK Government Foreign & Commonwealth Office, only essential travel will be permitted within the UK or overseas until 2 December 2020.
notes: Reverses the partial relaxation of 15 July. The 2 December end date matches the announced end of the second national lockdown.

headline: The Department for Education publishes Christmas travel guidance for students
detail: Published by the Department for Education and the Minister of State for Universities.
quote: University students will be able to travel home to spend Christmas with their families once the national restrictions end on 2 December, following steps set out in new Government guidance published today.
notes: The sector-specific counterpart to the second lockdown, and the reason UCL restricted travel to essential journeys until 2 December.

headline: Ramsay Hall becomes a COVID-19 testing centre for Camden residents
detail: A partnership between UCL, the London Borough of Camden and the Department of Health and Social Care, increasing testing capacity for the borough rather than for UCL.
quote: UCL’s Ramsay Hall will become a COVID-19 testing centre from today, as part of a partnership between the London Borough of Camden and the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC).
notes: UCL estate used for the borough's testing, not its own. Distinct from the Bidborough House centre for UCL students and staff, which opened a fortnight later.

headline: Asymptomatic lateral flow testing opens for students at Bidborough House
detail: Part of the national testing programme for universities, to support travel over the winter break. Free, voluntary, results in about two hours.
quote: Asymptomatic COVID-19 testing for UCL students starts today, as part of the national testing programme for universities to support students to travel over the winter break.
notes: Reverses the position of 16 September, when asymptomatic testing was ruled out as a routine offer. It arrives as a national programme with a specific purpose: getting students home.

headline: Staff explicitly excluded from asymptomatic testing at its launch
quote: If you are a member of UCL staff, please do not book an appointment for an asymptomatic test. The Government has introduced the national testing programme specifically to support students who wish to leave university for the end of term.
notes: Matters for reading the case data: through December 2020 the staff and student series were produced under different testing regimes, so a comparison between them in that period is not like for like.

headline: Monthly cases falls to 11 for students, on campus
detail: 43 in November 2020, 11 in December 2020, a change of -74%.
notes: Threshold: at least 50% and at least 25 cases, both from timeline.toml. Reported confirmed cases only, an undercount of unknown size. Testing intensity changed during the series: asymptomatic testing was ruled out in September 2020, opened to students in November 2020 and to staff in January 2021, and from 8 February 2021 a positive lateral flow test entered the count without PCR confirmation. "On campus" records a visit of 15 minutes or more in the two days before symptoms or a test, not where infection occurred.

headline: The second lockdown ends and England returns to the tier system
detail: London returned to Tier 2.
quote: Second lockdown ends after four weeks and England returns to a stricter three-tier system of restrictions

headline: Second national lockdown ends and London returns to Tier 2
quote: The current national lockdown period in England is due to end this Wednesday, 2 December, after which London will be in Tier 2 (High Alert) restrictions.
notes: London moved to Tier 3 on 16 December and Tier 4 on 20 December, neither of which the newsletters cover, because the last update before the winter break was 14 December. Both need retrieving in stage 2 to explain the December case peak.

headline: The student travel window opens
detail: A six-day window with staggered departure dates set by each university.
quote: From 3 December to 9 December, which will be known as the ‘student travel window’, students will be allowed to travel home on staggered departure dates set by universities, who will work with other institutions in the region to manage pressure on transport infrastructure.
notes: A national policy written specifically for universities, and one of the few that treats the student population as an epidemiological object in its own right.

headline: Coronavirus updates to pause from the start of Term 2
detail: In line with the Working Smarter initiative and feedback about email volume, with The Week@UCL continuing and coronavirus emails restarting only as needed.
quote: we are planning to pause these coronavirus emails from the start of next term. You will still receive The Week@UCL every Thursday, and we will restart these coronavirus emails as and when we need to share important information.
notes: The pause did not hold. Issue 129 followed on 5 January 2021, three weeks later, after the third national lockdown was announced. The intention to stop is itself evidence of how UCL read the situation in mid-December.

headline: Phased return of students planned for Term 2 on government guidance
detail: Departments prioritised practical, laboratory and studio subjects and early assessments, with students free to study remotely or on campus.
quote: Departments are writing to students today (Monday 14 December) with information about arrangements for the start of Term Two, in response to recent Government guidance about the phased return of students to universities across the country.
notes: Overtaken within three weeks by the third national lockdown. The plan for a phased return in January never happened as described.

headline: Student study spaces in former offices running at over 80% capacity
detail: Bidborough House, Torrington Place and 1 St Martin's Le Grand given over to study space and the national testing programme.
quote: These study spaces are currently operating at above 80% capacity, and the asymptomatic testing site is playing an important role in supporting our students to travel to and from London more safely.
notes: Evidence that on-campus presence in December 2020 was substantial and concentrated in study space rather than teaching, which is context for the December case figures.

headline: Tier 4 announced for London and the South East
detail: A new "Stay at Home" alert level, with the planned Christmas relaxation cut short.
quote: PM announces tougher restrictions for London and South East England, with a new Tier 4: ‘Stay at Home’ alert level. Christmas mixing rules tightened.
notes: The start of the phase in which UCL's January 2021 rise occurs. Attributing that rise to the Alpha variant is an epidemiological claim none of the cached sources makes, so it is not made here: what the ledger supports is that the restrictions tightened and the figures rose.

headline: Twice-weekly asymptomatic testing extended to staff working on campus
detail: At Bidborough House, free and voluntary, using lateral flow tests.
quote: UCL and contracted staff who are working on campus and who do not have COVID-19 symptoms are encouraged to get tested twice a week at UCL’s testing centre in Bidborough House.
notes: Five weeks after staff were told not to book asymptomatic tests. Encouraged on 5 January, expected by 18 January. A change in testing intensity that will show in the staff case counts independently of any change in infection.

headline: UCL responds to the third national lockdown: work from home if you can
detail: Campus stayed open for estates, libraries, cleaning, catering and security staff, and for researchers needing specialist facilities. Clinically extremely vulnerable staff told not to attend.
quote: If you can work from home during this period, you must do so . However, campus will remain open and some colleagues will be required to work onsite, for example, staff in our estates and libraries teams, and with our cleaning, catering and security partners.
notes: A one-day lag on the announcement of 4 January 2021. This is the policy under which UCL's on-campus student cases fell to their lowest point of the whole series in January 2021, which is the blog post's central claim.

headline: University staff classed as critical workers for school places
detail: Because universities were being asked to stay open and keep delivering learning, even remotely.
quote: Under the latest Government guidance, University staff are considered critical workers and are therefore eligible to send their children to school as usual. This is because we are being asked to keep universities open, and to continue to deliver learning (even if remotely).
notes: Qualified on 1 February: UCL clarified that critical worker status was mainly for school eligibility and did not itself justify travel.

headline: England enters the third national lockdown
detail: Announced by the Prime Minister on the evening of 4 January and in force from 6 January.
quote: England enters third national lockdown
notes: UCL responded on 5 January, between the announcement and the legal commencement. The ledger dates this row to the date this source gives, which is the commencement.

headline: 2 metre distancing mandated as the default in all settings
detail: Removing the flexibility previously allowed for critical laboratory work, which now needed Head of Department approval and a fresh risk assessment.
quote: In light of the recent increase in coronavirus cases and the tightening of Government restrictions, UCL is now mandating 2-metre social distancing as our default position in all settings, having provided some flexibility for critical lab-based activity if accompanied by a risk assessment.
notes: UCL tightening beyond its own July position, which had already been stricter than the national one metre plus.

headline: Government redefines a contact as 15 minutes cumulative within two metres
detail: Counting a single period or time accumulated over one day.
quote: Under the new guidance, this now includes anyone who has been within two metres of someone for more than 15 minutes, whether in a single period or cumulatively over the course of one day.
notes: The 15-minute threshold in the national contact definition. The on-campus marker in UCL's published data uses a similar 15-minute rule for presence, which is a different thing measured with a similar rule; do not conflate them.

headline: UCL legally required to report case figures to Camden Council and the OfS
detail: Alongside responding to cases, informing the testing programme and identifying outbreaks.
quote: report coronavirus case figures to Camden Council and the Office for Students, which we are legally required to do;
notes: The most important provenance fact about the dataset after the case definition itself. The numbers were not a voluntary publication: UCL had a statutory reporting duty to Camden and the OfS, and the public page sat on top of that obligation. The legal basis is a stage 2 retrieval target.

headline: All UK travel corridors removed and travel restricted to legally permitted reasons
detail: With faculty approval, a risk assessment, TravelCert registration, a negative test up to three days before departure and self-isolation on return.
quote: Staff and students should not travel unless it is for a legally permitted reason . Please note that from today the Government has announced there are no longer any travel corridors .
notes: The tightest travel position of the whole record, and the reversal of the partial reopening of 15 July 2020.

headline: All teaching to remain online for the rest of Term 2
detail: Except a small number of exempt courses, with a no-detriment package being developed for assessment.
quote: In response to the latest guidance from the UK Government , we are now planning for all teaching and other face-to-face activities to remain online for the remainder of Term Two, except for a small number of exempt courses.
notes: The decision that keeps the on-campus student line flat through the Alpha wave. Explicitly a response to national guidance rather than to UCL's own case counts.

headline: Free face masks provided for the commute of staff who must attend campus
detail: From 3 February to 8 March, collectable in Bloomsbury or posted to staff at outlying sites.
quote: UCL will be providing free face masks to wear during your commute from Wednesday 3 February until Monday 8 March when we will review the approach in line with Government guidance .
notes: UCL intervening in the journey to work, which is outside its estate and outside its control, because commuting was the concern staff reported most.

headline: Confirmatory PCR no longer required after a positive lateral flow test
detail: Isolation to begin from the day of the positive lateral flow result.
quote: In line with new Government guidance, anyone who has a positive LFT result no longer needs to take a confirmatory Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test afterwards.
notes: A change in what counts as a confirmed case, and therefore a change in the meaning of the published series partway through it. Lateral flow positives now enter the count without PCR confirmation.

headline: No detriment package published for 2020-21 assessment
detail: Developed with Students' Union UCL.
quote: UCL has today published details of its COVID-19 mitigation measures to support our students through their assessment in 2020-21. We have worked with Students’ Union UCL to develop a ‘no detriment’ package to make sure our students are not disadvantaged by the pandemic.
notes: The second year's version of the principle first adopted on 7 April 2020.

headline: The government publishes the roadmap out of lockdown
detail: Four steps, replacing the regional tier system with uniform national easing.
quote: PM publishes a roadmap for lifting the lockdown
notes: UCL published its own roadmap tracking these four steps on 23 March 2021.

headline: Government roadmap allows practical teaching to resume from 8 March
detail: A four-step roadmap announced on 22 February, with higher education guidance limited at first to practical and practice-based courses needing specialist facilities.
quote: Universities can resume in-person teaching for students on practical or practice-based courses and who require specialist equipment and facilities from 8 March.
notes: Filed on 22 February, the date of the announcement; UCL reported it on 23 February, a one-day lag. The 8 March date is the first loosening for universities since the January lockdown, and it is narrow.

headline: Practical and practice-based teaching resumes on campus
detail: Eligible students contacted directly through their programmes.
quote: As part of the Government’s four-step roadmap to ease lockdown restrictions, from 8 March 2021 UCL can resume in-person teaching for students on practical or practice-based courses and who require specialist equipment.
notes: Filed on 8 March, the effective date; announced 2 March. The blog post notes the shaded campus-closed period running to 17 May 2021, so this partial return sits inside it and should be shown as such rather than as a reopening.

headline: One year of remote working measured in platform use
quote: in the last year, UCL has had 530 Zoom sessions, nearly 40,000 Lecturecast recordings, more than 1.5 million meetings on MS Teams, and over 16 million daily logins on Moodle during term-time
notes: The Zoom figure of 530 is almost certainly wrong by orders of magnitude: issue 119 alone recorded over 2,800 Zoom sessions in a single day in October 2020. Quoted as printed and flagged; do not repeat the 530 figure as a fact.

headline: Future of Work survey opened on what should return to campus
detail: A seven-question survey open until 18 April 2021 on what worked remotely and what belongs on site.
quote: What you tell us now will help us decide what areas we should invest in for our future, what changes we should make to how we work and how we can optimise our workspaces to deliver UCL’s ambitions for years to come.
notes: The first question in the record about what should be permanent rather than what should be endured.

headline: UCL publishes its own roadmap tracking the government's four steps
detail: More campus spaces from 12 April including fitness, study space and outdoor dining, with a hoped-for full return no earlier than 21 June.
quote: We are now creating our own version of the roadmap for the university, underpinned by our people-first approach and commitment to maintaining our symptom-free testing service and the Connect to Protect reporting tool.
notes: UCL committing to keep its own testing and reporting running through the reopening, which is why the case series continues past the point where campus restrictions ease.

headline: Free rapid testing opens to everyone in England
detail: UCL encouraged twice-weekly use and kept its own Bidborough House centre for those who needed to be on campus.
quote: The Government have announced that access to free, regular, rapid coronavirus testing will be available to everyone in England from 9 April .
notes: Filed on 9 April, the national effective date; reported by UCL on 12 April. From this point UCL's own testing provision is a convenience rather than a necessity, which changes what its case counts are capturing.

headline: UCL relays advice that COVID tests do not invalidate the Ramadan fast
detail: From the Department of Health and Social Care in consultation with the British Islamic Medical Association.
quote: Their position is that LFT and PCR COVID tests do not invalidate the Ramadan fast.
notes: A testing-uptake measure aimed at a specific community, on the first day of Ramadan 2021.

headline: Remaining students told to stay away until in-person teaching resumes on 17 May
detail: With an exception for students whose mental health or wellbeing was affecting their ability to study.
quote: Students should remain where they are to continue with their studies and not return to term-time accommodation before their face-to-face teaching resumes, unless they have mental health or wellbeing challenges impacting on their ability to study successfully.
notes: An instruction not to return, which is why the on-campus student line stays flat through spring 2021 even as national restrictions eased.

headline: UCL sets a three-step return: 17 May, 21 June, then September
detail: Students and paused research from 17 May, campus fully open from 21 June, majority of staff back for part of the week from September.
quote: In line with Government guidance, all remaining staff will be able to start returning to onsite working from 21 June, ahead of the start of the 2021/22 academic year.
notes: Explicitly built on three inputs: the government roadmap, UCL's own public health experts, and staff feedback. The 21 June date later slipped by four weeks with the national step 4 delay.

headline: All remaining students may return to campus and face-to-face teaching restarts
detail: With parking, FFP2 masks, symptom-free testing and Connect to Protect offered as practical support.
quote:
From Monday 17 May all remaining students who have been
studying remotely can return to campus (including paused research projects),
and face-to-face teaching and supervision can restart.
notes: The end of the campus-closed period the blog post shades on its student figure, which runs January to 17 May 2021. Filed on 17 May, the effective date; announced 4 May.

headline: Travel permitted to Green and Amber list countries for essential reasons
detail: With quarantine costs met by UCL or the grant where travel was essential, and flexible tickets required.
quote: Staff and students may now travel on UCL business to countries that are on the Green or Amber lists for essential reasons.
notes: The first loosening since travel corridors were removed on 18 January 2021.

headline: Future of Work survey finds most staff want lasting flexibility
detail: Just over a third of staff responded. More than half reported an improved work-life blend, with commuting less and the financial effect named as gains.
quote: more than half of staff reported an overall improvement in their work-life blend and colleagues said they enjoy commuting less and the positive financial impact
notes: The evidence base for the 40% on-campus expectation set in the same issue. Response rate is stated as just over a third, so the finding is not a census.

headline: Staff to spend a minimum of 40% of working time on campus from September
detail: With the exact proportion depending on role and departmental need, and no staff required to work remotely.
quote: we will typically expect all colleagues to spend a minimum of 40% of their working time onsite from September
notes: The permanent settlement that came out of the pandemic, and the first policy in the record framed around what work should look like afterwards rather than during.

headline: Step 4 of the roadmap delayed by four weeks to 19 July
detail: Delayed in response to the Delta variant.
quote: delayed by four weeks, until 19 July, as the government accelerates the vaccination programme.
notes: UCL's return timetable slipped with it, which is the clearest case in the record of a UCL date moving purely because a national date moved.

headline: Step 4 delayed four weeks and UCL's return timetable slips with it
detail: From 21 June to 19 July, with staff asked to keep working remotely until at least that date.
quote: The Government announced last night that stage four in the roadmap to ease lockdown restrictions will be delayed by four weeks, from Monday 21 June to Monday 19 July.
notes: Filed on 14 June, the date of the announcement; UCL reported it on 15 June, a one-day lag. The clearest case of a UCL date moving purely because a national date moved.

headline: Staff asked to report every test result, positive or negative, to Connect to Protect
quote: Once you receive your results, whether positive or negative, you should report your results through the NHS and through UCL’s Connect to Protect tool .
notes: UCL asking for negatives as well as positives, though only confirmed positives reach the published page. The denominator was collected but never published, which is why a positivity rate cannot be recovered from the archive.

headline: UCL encourages students to register with a GP so they can be invited for vaccination
quote: We are encouraging students to register with a GP so they can be invited to book their vaccination as the rollout continues and they become eligible.
notes: A practical obstacle specific to students: eligibility depended on GP registration, and students often were not registered locally.

headline: Step 4 removes most legal limits on social contact in England
detail: The end of the legal requirements, including distancing and face coverings.
quote: Most legal limits on social contact removed
notes: UCL kept face coverings in all indoor spaces a week later, and this ends the 2 metre rule UCL had held since 8 July 2020.

headline: One-way systems removed and social distancing relaxed at step 4
detail: Most spaces returned to normal capacity, with face coverings still expected in crowded indoor areas.
quote: All remaining one-way systems will be removed and social distancing requirements will be relaxed, which will mean most spaces can return to their normal capacity.
notes: Filed on 19 July, the effective date; announced 13 July. The end of the 2 metre rule UCL had held since 8 July 2020, sixteen months earlier, including through a period when the national rule was one metre plus.

headline: Face coverings kept in all indoor spaces after legal restrictions ended
detail: Including lectures, seminar rooms, study spaces, offices and laboratories.
quote: Unless you are exempt, we expect everyone on campus to wear a face covering in indoor spaces, including in lectures, seminar rooms, study spaces, offices and labs.
notes: A second deliberate divergence from national policy in the cautious direction, a year after the 2 metre decision. Legal requirements had ended a week earlier.

headline: Pilot Remote Working Policy published with hybrid working guidance
quote: A new pilot Remote Working Policy and set of hybrid working FAQs have been produced to support existing guidance and policies on working from home and on campus, during the pandemic, including key dates and the expectations of our staff.

headline: Testing centre moves from Bidborough House to the Student Centre at reduced scale
detail: Bidborough House closed on 30 July, with a smaller service opening at the Student Centre for those who preferred to test on site or needed help.
quote: The Lateral Flow Testing (LFT) centre on the ground floor of Bidborough House will close on Friday 30 July. A new LFT facility is due to open at the UCL Student Centre on Monday 2 August, providing a smaller-scale service
notes: A reduction in UCL's own testing capacity, once home tests were universally available. Filed on 2 August, the opening date of the replacement.

headline: Your Wellbeing survey folded into a weekly People Pulse survey
detail: After just over a year, with a one-year review published.
quote: From Monday 2 August, the Your Wellbeing survey will be phased into the weekly People Pulse survey, to help us understand how our staff are coping as we transition into hybrid working.
notes: The crisis instrument becomes a permanent one. The survey ran weekly from 22 June 2020, which is longer than the published case series.

headline: Collection outage of 50 hours
detail: The hourly scraper stopped for 50 hours, so any page updates in that window were not captured.
notes: The collection had a 50-hour outage from 2021-08-21 08:34 to 2021-08-23 10:34 caused by the git corruption incident. Any data-track claim spanning this window carries this caveat. The published figures are cumulative, so totals recover; daily readings within the window do not.

headline: Face covering policy reviewed by senior management and deliberately kept
detail: Staff had raised concerns about wearing coverings all day, and the Senior Management Team decided to maintain the requirement pending a further review on 22 October.
quote: However, we have determined that our current approach should be maintained, because it is an important way to help keep our community as safe as possible as larger numbers of staff and students return to campus.
notes: A documented decision rather than a default, which is what makes it usable as evidence that UCL chose to stay stricter than the law required.

headline: NHS vaccination centre opens at UCL's Bidborough House
detail: Run by UCLH staff in partnership with UCL, open to local residents and students for first or second doses, bookable through the national system.
quote: An NHS vaccination centre has been opened at UCL’s Bidborough House site on Mabledon Place, off Euston Road, giving local residents and students the ability to book an appointment in the heart of Camden.
notes: The same building that housed the asymptomatic testing centre, and before that staff offices given over to student study space. The third repurposing of one building in a year.

headline: COVID-19 Visitor Policy withdrawn
detail: Visitors still signed in but were no longer required to declare symptoms or register the areas they visited.
quote: The COVID-19 Visitor Policy is no longer in effect.
notes: Ends the contact-tracing regime for visitors introduced on 24 August 2020.

headline: Department for Education says students may decline face coverings
detail: Setting departmental guidance against UCL's own expectation that everyone wear one indoors.
quote: Although this is UCL’s position, the Department for Education has said that students can choose not to wear face coverings and they must not miss out on educational sessions if they do so.
notes: An explicit conflict between UCL policy and national guidance, stated in the newsletter. UCL kept its expectation but could not enforce it against students, which is the clearest limit on institutional autonomy anywhere in the record.

headline: Ventilation reworked across campus with a CO2 monitoring trial
detail: Air recirculation turned off in mechanically ventilated rooms, full fresh air supplied, maintenance brought forward before the autumn term.
quote: In rooms with mechanical ventilation, air recirculation has been turned off and full fresh air is being supplied;
notes: A physical infection-control measure rather than a behavioural one, and the only one in the record that changed the buildings themselves.

headline: All remaining staff expected back on campus from the start of term
detail: With an expectation of at least 40% of working time on site, agreed individually with line managers.
quote: From the start of term on 27 September, UCL expects all remaining staff to return to work from our buildings.
notes: Filed on 27 September, the effective date; announced 14 September. Eighteen months after the closure of 20 March 2020, and the point at which campus population returns to something like normal — which is the context for the Omicron peak three months later.

headline: Face coverings expected during classroom teaching for the new academic year
detail: With no evidence required from anyone exempt, and a review scheduled for 22 October 2021.
quote: All staff, students and visitors are expected to wear face coverings whilst indoors in all UCL buildings including during classroom teaching, unless they are exempt.
notes: The policy in force at the start of the academic year that ends with the Omicron peak of December 2021.

notes: Filed on 22 October, the date of the review; reported 25 October. The second documented decision to stay stricter than the law required.

headline: Traffic light travel system replaced by a Red List of seven countries
detail: UCL permitted business travel to any country not on the Red List where the need was justified.

notes: The loosest travel position since March 2020. It lasted five weeks before Omicron.

headline: All UCL-sponsored staff social gatherings cancelled

headline: UCL states cases are rising on campus as well as nationally

This is the passage quoted in the blog post.

headline: On-campus student cases: 9 in January 2021, 696 in January 2022
detail: The same calendar month under opposite campus policies. In January 2021 all teaching was online and students were told not to return; in January 2022 campus was open for face-to-face teaching under the higher education exemption from Plan B.
notes: The blog post's central claim, computed rather than asserted. It shows that the on-campus line moved with policy, not that policy caused the difference: national prevalence also differed between the two months, and reported confirmed cases only, an undercount of unknown size. testing intensity changed during the series: asymptomatic testing was ruled out in september 2020, opened to students in november 2020 and to staff in january 2021, and from 8 february 2021 a positive lateral flow test entered the count without pcr confirmation. "On campus" records a visit of 15 minutes or more in the two days before symptoms or a test, not where infection occurred.

headline: UCL rises 77-fold between the two Januaries, Camden 2.4-fold
detail: Camden recorded 4,770 cases in January 2021 and 11,211 in January 2022, a factor of 2.4. UCL on-campus students went from 9 to 696, a factor of 77 — about 33 times the borough's growth.
notes: The sharpest test of the blog post's claim available, and it does not say what a first glance suggests. **Both** rose: the borough's epidemic grew 2.4-fold between the two months, so a purely epidemiological account does predict a rise at UCL. What it does not predict is the size: UCL rose about 33 times as steeply as the borough around it. That gap is the evidence, not a difference in direction. The plain reading is that the local epidemic accounts for part of the change and campus policy for the rest — closed to most students in January 2021, open in January 2022. UCL cases are not a subset of Camden cases: students live across many boroughs and "on campus" marks presence, not residence. Shape and timing may be compared; shares and proportions may not.

quote: The Government has removed remaining domestic COVID-19 restrictions in England and has published advice on living safely with respiratory infections including COVID-19 , which includes measures such as getting vaccinated, keeping spaces well-ventilated and practicing good hygiene.
notes: Issue 165, the last of the 168 files. It is not on UCL's index page and was fetched separately; manifest.csv records this.

headline: Twice-weekly testing advice dropped as free national testing ends
quote: In line with Government guidance and the end of the free national testing programme, we no longer advise staff and students to test for COVID-19 twice a week.
notes: The end of routine testing, and therefore of the mechanism that generated the case data. The published series stops a week later, on 11 May 2022, which is the reason the record ends: the counting stopped, not the pandemic.

headline: The published case series ends
